It's about three kilometers from here to the coast.
That's fine. Let's leave enough time to get back before dark.
Could we eat near the harbor so we don't have to drive again?
Yes, I'll find a place within walking distance of the car park.
I'll bring a warm jacket in case it's windy by the water.

l2-016.title: Thinking about changing jobs.
signature: You asked me to look at your résumé. What's changed?
Let's talk about the kind of work you'd enjoy before we edit it.
I like helping people, but I'd rather work predictable hours.
Then look for roles that list the shifts clearly.
I'll compare two adverts and see which of my skills they ask for.

l2-017.title: The last person to leave.
signature: I'll stay in the study room for a few more minutes.
Be sure to turn off the light when you leave the room.
I will. I'll lock the door as well.
Thanks. Before you lock up, check that the back window is shut.
I checked it earlier, but I'll look again on my way out.
Leave the key in the drop box so the morning team can get in.

l2-018.title: Working out how the lock works.
signature: Could you open this locker for me?
I have no idea how it works.
Try turning the knob after entering the code. I can show you.
Should I hear a click before I turn it?
Yes, and the green light should come on at the same time.
I see it now; let me try once on my own.

l2-019.title: Finding someone to help with maths.
signature: Can you help me check these fractions?
Great. Could you show me one example before I try the rest?
Sure; let's start by writing the numbers in the same units.
So should I turn the metres into centimetres first?
Yes. After that, add them and check that your answer is reasonable.

l2-020.title: Moving to a quieter room.
signature: There are too many people in this room.
The small room at the end of the corridor is free.
Let's go there so everyone can hear.
Do we need to tell the people who haven't arrived yet?
Yes, send the new room number to the group.
I'll leave a note on this door too, in case someone misses the message.

l2-021.title: Returning to French practice.
signature: Would you like to join us for a short conversation in French?
It's been a long time since I last spoke French.
We'll start with introductions. You can listen to the first round.
I can still remember a little French.
Try ordering something simple without looking at your notes.
All right, and next time you can ask me a follow-up question.

l2-022.title: Keeping your bedtime routine away from home.
signature: Should I put the toiletries in the suitcase now?
I always brush my teeth before I go to bed.
I'll leave your toothbrush out and pack it in the morning.
Could you leave it in the cup by the sink?
Sure, and I'll put your bag by the door as a reminder.
Thanks. I'll set my alarm so I have time to pack after breakfast.

l2-023.title: Checking on a friend's plans.
signature: I'm sorry I didn't answer your message. My battery died.
I was worried you wouldn't come.
I'm here now. Did you already order, or shall we look at the menu?
I waited for you because I wasn't sure how hungry you'd be.
Let's share a main dish and get a side salad.
Good idea; I'll ask how big the portions are.

l2-024.title: Asking for more preparation time.
signature: Are you ready to present the draft?
I need a little more time to prepare.
That's fine. Take ten minutes and tell us when you're ready.
Can someone check the projector while I finish the slides?
I'll connect it now and leave the first slide on the screen.
Thanks; I'll start with that slide as soon as the others sit down.

l2-025.title: Checking who went on the trip.
signature: Did Tom and Mary take the train to Boston?
Neither Tom nor Mary went to Boston.
Then let's ask who booked the seats before we change the reservation.
I have the email here; Mariam made the booking.
Could she check whether the fare allows a name change?
I'll ask her before we promise the spare seat to anyone.

l2-026.title: A result you are pleased with.
signature: How do you feel about the final layout?
I'm happy with the way things turned out.
So am I. Shall we send it to the rest of the team?
Yes, but let's show the figures we used to reach it.
Good point; I'll attach the table and explain which entries we left out.
I'll read the note once before you send it.

l2-027.title: A glass of water while waiting.
signature: Would you like something to drink while you wait?
Of course. I'll bring you a glass.
Thank you; is it all right if I take it into the meeting room?
Yes, but leave the glass on the tray when you're done.
I will. Is the tray on the table just inside?

l2-028.title: Wondering about tomorrow's weather.
signature: I wonder if it will rain tomorrow.
Let's set a table inside too, in case the weather changes.
Should we let everyone know we may move indoors?
Yes, mention that the start time won't change.
I'll add directions to the side entrance in the same message.

l2-029.title: Talking about a place you've never visited.
signature: What was your first trip to the States like?
I have never been to the States.
I must have mixed you up with someone else. Where did you go last year?
I went to a smaller town by the coast instead.
Was it easy to get around without a car?
Yes, I used the bus in the morning and walked back by the sea.

l2-030.title: Making time for reading.
signature: How do you finish a book every week?
I spend a lot of time reading.
Could I start with twenty minutes after dinner?
That should work, but choose a time when you won't be interrupted.
I'll read after I clear the table and leave my phone in the kitchen.
Try it for a week and see whether you want a longer session.

l2-031.title: Correcting yourself in a meeting.
signature: The email says the workshop is on Thursday, not Tuesday.
Thanks for checking. I'll correct the calendar invitation.
Could you add a note explaining why the time has changed?
Yes, some people are still looking at the old agenda.
I'll send them the new agenda separately so they can prepare.

l2-032.title: A decision that needs a conversation.
signature: Can we confirm the new schedule today?
I can't make that decision without talking to Tom first.
All right. I'll keep both options open until you've spoken to him.
I'll call him at lunch and ask which day he can cover.
Can you confirm the answer before four?
Yes; if I can't reach him, I'll tell you before then.

l2-033.title: A new French practice agreement.
signature: We keep switching to English when the exercises get harder.
From now on, we'll only speak French.
Agreed. If I get stuck, I'll try to explain the word in French.
And if I don't understand, I'll ask you to say it another way.
Shall we write down the words we had trouble with afterwards?
Yes, we'll use those words to start our next conversation.

l2-034.title: Waiting for a reply.
signature: Is there anything else you can send with the application?
All I can do at the moment is wait.
Then let's put a reminder in the calendar for next week.
What should I do if the reply arrives while I'm away?
Forward it to me if it needs a decision before you get back.
All right, I'll tell the sender who to contact while I'm gone.

l2-035.title: When more thinking makes it harder.
signature: Have you worked out what the last question is asking?
The more I think about it, the less I understand it.
Let's try a small example and see what changes.
Let's test it with only two items so we can follow each step.
Then we can add a third item and see where the problem starts.
I'll note what we changed so we don't repeat the same test.

l2-036.title: Waiting in the right place.
signature: Is this the queue for the reception desk?
I was told to wait here.
You're in the right place. They'll call your name when it's your turn.
Can I go and get water while I wait?
Yes, the fountain is just round the corner; you should still hear them.
I'll take my bag with me and come straight back.

l2-037.title: Getting ready to resume work.
signature: Would you like another few minutes before we start?
I'm ready to get back to work.
Great. We'll go through the two remaining requests together.
Which one needs an answer today?
The booking request; we can deal with the other one tomorrow.
I'll open the booking calendar so we can check the available dates.

l2-038.title: Identifying an unfamiliar fruit.
signature: What is this fruit next to the lemons?
It does. Let's ask the seller what it is before we buy it.
Excuse me, is this fruit ready to eat or does it need a few days?
This one is ripe; the firmer ones will keep longer.
I'll take a ripe one to try and a firm one for the weekend.

l2-039.title: A call as soon as you get home.
signature: The bus is here. I'll head home now.
Call me as soon as you get home.
I will. It should take about twenty minutes.
If you stop at the shop, just send me a quick message.
I don't need anything tonight, so I'll come straight home.
All right, I'll keep my phone nearby until I hear from you.

l2-040.title: Choosing a quiet evening activity.
signature: Shall I put on the television?
I prefer reading books to watching television.
I'll turn it off then. Could you recommend a book?
Try the short stories on the top shelf; you can finish one tonight.
Are any of them set near the sea?
The first story is; start there and tell me what you think tomorrow.

l2-041.title: Welcoming a visitor.
signature: I made it just before the doors closed.
I'm glad I could make it. Where should I put my coat?
Hang it by the door, and leave your bag on the bench.
Thanks. I brought some dates; shall I put them in the kitchen?
Yes, let's serve them with tea after everyone arrives.

l2-042.title: Handling the important task first.
signature: Could you call the client before lunch? They need to confirm the address.
Since it's important, I'll do it.
Thanks. Let me know if the delivery point has changed.
It has; take the boxes to the back door this time.
Do I need to call before I unload them?
Yes, call when you arrive so someone can open the gate.

l2-043.title: Giving credit for an idea.
signature: Whose idea was it to add a map to the welcome pack?
I'm the one who came up with the idea.
Good idea. Could you show the new team how it works?
Sure, I'll use a real example and explain what she changed.
Invite her too in case they have questions about the original idea.
I'll ask her which part she'd like to present herself.

l2-044.title: A short business trip.
signature: Where did you go for your meeting last week?
I went to Boston for five days on a business trip.
Did you have time to visit the city after the meetings?
Only for an hour. I walked around the old market near my hotel.
Would you stay in the same area next time?
Yes, I could walk to the meetings and still find somewhere to eat afterwards.

l2-045.title: Choosing how to get there.
signature: Would it be easier if you rented a car?
I don't know how to drive a car.
Then let's share a taxi from the station.
Where should we wait for each other?
Meet under the big clock; it's easy to see from the platforms.
Good, and if my train is late, I'll message you before you book the taxi.

l2-046.title: Shopping with priorities.
signature: Do you want to buy everything on this list today?
I don't have enough money to buy everything I need.
Let's get the basics today and leave the rest for next week.
Can we leave the juice and buy fruit instead?
Yes, check what's in season so we stay within the budget.
The oranges are cheaper this week; I'll get enough for breakfast.

l2-047.title: Returning to a closed shop.
signature: The repair shop has closed early. What will you do?
I plan to come back tomorrow.
I'll check when it opens and send you the time.
Could you check if they close for lunch too?
Yes, and I'll ask whether the item is still in stock.
Thanks; if it's sold out, I'll try the branch near work.

l2-048.title: Adjusting an activity for a smaller class.
signature: Half of the students are absent.
Then we can make two groups instead of four.
Good. I'll give each group a different question.
Should each group report back after five minutes?
Give them eight; they need time to agree on one answer.
All right, I'll ask each group to choose someone to speak.

l2-049.title: Encouraging someone to ask.
signature: I'm still getting used to the office.
Don't hesitate to ask if you want anything.
Thanks. Could you show me where the spare stationery is?
The paper is in this drawer; what else are you looking for?
I need an envelope large enough for these forms.
Try one from the bottom shelf; you won't have to fold the forms.

l2-050.title: Opening a gift together.
signature: Is it all right if I open this now?
Go ahead and unwrap your gift.
Thank you. I'll open it carefully so I can keep the paper.
You can pull this ribbon loose instead of cutting it.
Oh, it's a notebook! Is this the one you saw at the fair?
Yes, the seller made it by hand and left the pages blank for sketches.

l2-051.title: How long have you studied French.
signature: How many years have you been studying French?
I've been studying French for three years.
Then you'll be fine in the conversation group. We meet on Thursdays.
Do I need to understand everything people say?
At this time, you don't need to understand everything.
Then I'll focus on catching the main idea and ask about new words afterwards.

l2-052.title: Finding a way to wind down.
signature: For some reason, I'm wide awake and can't fall asleep.
Let's move tomorrow's early meeting so you have more time to rest.
Could we move it to eleven instead of ten?
Eleven is fine; I'll tell the others so no one comes early.
Thanks, I'll turn off my phone once the new time is confirmed.

l2-053.title: Looking for a flat near work.
signature: I'm looking for an apartment to rent.
Do you want to live near work or near the station?
Near the station, as long as it's on a quiet street.
There's a flat two streets back; do you want to see it after work?
Yes, and I'd like to hear how noisy it is at that time of day.
I'll ask to visit before sunset so we can check the light as well.

l2-054.title: Making room for a guest.
signature: The guest room isn't ready yet. Would you prefer to stay at a hotel?
I don't mind sleeping on the couch.
Then I'll bring you a blanket and clear the table beside it.
Thanks. Is there a socket nearby for my phone?
Yes, it's behind the small table; I'll move the lamp a little.
That's fine; my cable is long enough to reach it now.

l2-055.title: Thanking someone for their help.
signature: I left a few notes so you can use the new booking system tomorrow.
I can't tell you how much I appreciate your help.
You're welcome. Call me if you get stuck.
I'll try it myself first and note down where I have trouble.
Good plan. A screenshot might help me see what's happening.
I'll send one if the same error comes up again.

l2-056.title: Remembering an old bridge.
signature: Why is the path here wider than the path on the other side?
At one time, there was a bridge here.
That makes sense. Is there a photo of the bridge anywhere?
Yes, there's one in the album with my grandparents' photos.
Can you tell when it was taken?
There's a date on the back; I can check it when I get home.

l2-057.title: Avoiding the same mistake twice.
signature: Why did you check the address twice before sending the parcel?
I didn't want to make the same mistake twice.
Good idea. Let's add that check to the packing list.
Should we check the charger when we check the laptop?
Yes, put them next to each other on the list.
I'll also add a box we can tick once each item is packed.

l2-058.title: Getting to know a new colleague.
signature: I'll show you where we keep the meeting notes.
By the way, where are you from?
I'm from Muscat. I moved here last month.
How are you finding the journey to work?
It's easy on the bus, but I haven't found a good place for lunch yet.
I'll show you the bakery across the street during our break.

l2-059.title: Talking about work you're proud of.
signature: Which project would you like to tell us about?
Could you choose one example and explain your role in it?
I made a guide that helped new staff answer common questions.
How did you decide which questions to include?
I asked three new colleagues what they had struggled to explain.

l2-060.title: Making a visitor feel included.
signature: I'll introduce our guest to everyone in French.
Keep in mind that Tom doesn't speak French very well.
Good point. I'll introduce him in English and translate the names of the activities.
Should we pair him with someone during the first activity?
Yes, I'll ask a volunteer to explain the steps as they go.
And I'll check with him at the break to see how it's going.

l2-061.title: Comparing two cities.
signature: Have you been to Boston or Chicago in the past three weeks?
Yes, I was in both cities last month.
In some ways, Boston is nicer than Chicago.
What did you like most about Boston?
I could walk to the shops and the library from my flat.
That's something I miss too; here I usually need the bus.

l2-062.title: Offering help with luggage.
signature: I can't carry both bags up these stairs at once.
Let me help you with your suitcases.
Thanks. Could you take the larger one?
Of course. Does it have anything fragile inside?
Yes, keep it upright; the glass is wrapped in a towel.
I'll hold it by the sides when we go up the stairs.

l2-063.title: Checking whose office it is.
signature: I left a parcel in your office, beside the blue cabinet.
I didn't say this was my office.
You're right. I'll check the name on the door before I fetch it.
If it's not there, ask reception before you open another room.
Good idea; the office numbers look almost the same from here.
I'll come with you and read the number on the list.

l2-064.title: Trying out a new camera.
signature: Is that the camera you were saving for?
I bought a camera the other day.
Let's try it by the window where there's more light.
Could you stand a little farther back so I can get the whole picture?
Here? Try tapping the screen to focus on my face.
That helped. Now let's see how it does when I move the camera.

l2-065.title: Catching up on unfinished homework.
signature: Can you show me your answers to the homework?
To tell the truth, I didn't do my homework.
You can work through the first two questions now and finish the rest tonight.
Can you go over the first question with me before I start?
Sure, read it aloud and tell me what it asks you to find.
I think it asks for a reason, not just the final answer.

l2-066.title: Recommending a favourite book.
signature: I'm thinking of borrowing this novel. Have you read it?
That's one of my favorite books.
Then I'll give it a try. Could you tell me which part you liked?
I liked the chapter where the family has to decide whether to move.
Do I need to read from the beginning to understand it?
Yes, but the chapters are short; I finished the first two on the bus.

l2-067.title: Explaining a change of plan.
signature: Did you get to the market this morning?
Because of the rain, I could not go out.
We can go together after it stops.
What if the rain lasts until the shop closes?
Then let's order what we need and go tomorrow for the rest.
I'll check what we already have before we place an order.

l2-068.title: Giving directions after a wrong turn.
signature: You arrived from the back street. Did the directions help?
I had a hard time finding his house.
Next time, use the park entrance as a landmark. I'll send you a pin.
Is that the entrance beside the playground?
No, use the one opposite the bus stop; the path is shorter from there.
Got it. I'll save that location in case I lose my signal.

l2-069.title: Making an early start a habit.
signature: How do you find time to practise before work?
I make it a rule to get up early in the morning.
I'll try getting up twenty minutes earlier on weekdays.
What will you do with the extra time in the morning?
I'll eat breakfast at home instead of buying something on the way.
Try getting breakfast ready the night before so it's easy to stick with.

l2-070.title: Asking someone to speak more clearly.
signature: The gate has changed. You'll need to use the walkway on the left.
Of course. Turn left here and follow the signs for gate eight.
Is gate eight before or after the security desk?
After it. Walk past the desk, then take the first right.
Thanks, that's much clearer. I'll look for the signs after the desk.

l2-071.title: Walking despite the rain.
signature: Did the rain spoil your afternoon in the park?
Even though it was raining, we decided to take a walk.
Then you must have found a sheltered path. Where did you go?
We took the path under the trees, but the ground was still wet.
Would you take the same route if it rained again?
I'd use the paved path next time; my shoes took hours to dry.

l2-072.title: A rainbow after the storm.
signature: What did you see as soon as the rain stopped?
No sooner had it stopped raining than a beautiful rainbow appeared.
That's why everyone stepped outside with their cameras.
Could you see it from the front of the building?
Only part of it; the best view was from the steps at the back.
I'll remember that spot the next time the sun comes out after rain.

l2-073.title: Talking about the length of a stay.
signature: Do you plan to stay long?
I intend to stay in Boston for three days.
Then you have time for the museum and a walk by the river.
Which one should I do first if it might rain later?
Walk by the river now and save the museum for the afternoon.
Good idea; I'll check the last entry time before I set off.

l2-074.title: Noticing more on each reading.
signature: Why are you reading the same book again?
Every time I read this book, I find something new.
I'll try that with a shorter story and make a note of what I notice.
What will you look for the first time you read it?
I'll work out what happens, then look for clues about how the characters feel.
Try comparing your notes with someone who read it too.

l2-075.title: Finishing a task earlier than expected.
signature: Did you have enough time to finish the report?
I was able to finish the work earlier than I had expected.
Great. Please show me how you organised your notes.
I put the questions in one column and the answers beside them.
Did you leave space for anything you couldn't answer?
Yes, I marked those rows and asked the team to check them.

l2-076.title: Finding lost keys in an unexpected place.
signature: Did you check the coat you wore yesterday?
Where were they? I'll put a small bowl there so we have a regular place for them.
They were in my jacket pocket, not on the shelf.
Then let's put the bowl by the coat hooks so we see it when we come in.

l2-077.title: Falling asleep while listening.
signature: Did you hear the end of the radio interview last night?
I fell asleep while listening to the radio.
I'll send you the recording so you can hear the last part.
Thanks. Do you know where the speaker starts talking about the trip?
At about twelve minutes; I'll send you the exact point.
Great, I'll listen from there while I walk to work.

l2-078.title: Knowing someone since school.
signature: How long have you known Tom?
I've known Tom since high school.
Then you must have plenty of stories from your school days.
We once put on a play with only two days to practise.
Did you both have speaking parts?
I did, but she worked backstage and reminded me of my lines.

l2-079.title: Whose turn is it to take out the rubbish.
signature: We have to put the bin outside before seven.
It's my turn to take out the trash.
Thanks. I'll bring the empty bin back in the morning.
Can you rinse it before you put it away?
Yes, I'll leave it in the sun until it's dry.
Thanks; there are spare bin bags under the sink.

l2-080.title: Checking if someone is still there.
signature: I'm here, but I was just about to leave.
I was wondering if you were still here.
I can stay for another minute. What do you need?
Could you check whether I left my notebook on your desk?
There's a blue one here with a pencil inside.
That's mine; please leave it at reception so I can collect it later.

l2-081.title: Working out a machine's controls.
signature: This is the printer we can use for labels.
Choose the label size first. I'll print one as an example.
How do I stop it from printing a whole sheet?
Set the quantity to one and check the preview.
I see just one label now; I'll use these settings for the next order.

l2-082.title: Reporting a question about travel.
signature: What did you ask her about before booking the trip?
I asked her if she had been to Mexico.
What did she say? I'd like some advice before we choose a route.
She said the coast road was slower but had more places to stop.
Then we could take it on the way there and use the main road back.
Good plan; I'll choose a place for lunch along the coast.

l2-083.title: Understanding a sentence in a book.
signature: I don't understand what this sentence means.
Which word is causing the problem?
The word after the verb. Can we try a simpler example?
Try this one: she looked up the word in a dictionary.
So looked up means she searched for it, not that she raised her eyes?
Exactly; now read the original sentence with that meaning in mind.

l2-084.title: Looking back on a missed lecture.
signature: The tutor explained that point at yesterday's lecture.
I ought to have attended the lecture.
I've got the notes. Let's go through the section you missed.
Thanks, I understood the first part but missed the example with the graph.
Start with the labels on the two axes and then read the numbers.
Now I can see why the line goes down after the second point.

l2-085.title: Allowing more time for a repair.
signature: Can the technician finish the repair by lunch?
It'll likely take much longer than you expect.
Then let's keep the spare printer available until tomorrow.
Can we move it to the front desk so everyone can reach it?
Yes, I'll connect it there and print a test page.
I'll put up a note telling people where to collect their printouts.

l2-086.title: Finding exactly the right item.
signature: Here is a smaller bag with the same strap.
That's what I was looking for.
Great. Would you like to check that your laptop fits?
Yes, I'd like to check there's space for the charger too.
Use the front pocket so the plug doesn't press against the screen.
That works. I'll take this bag and keep the receipt in case I need it.

l2-087.title: Getting ready for a trip.
signature: Can you join us for coffee this afternoon?
I'm busy getting ready for my trip.
No problem. Send me a message when you're back.
I will. Could you also check the mail while I'm away?
Of course; where should I put anything that looks urgent?
Send me a photo of the envelope and I'll tell you what to do.

l2-088.title: Getting used to a new neighbourhood.
signature: How are you settling into the new flat?
I'm starting to get used to living here.
Would you like me to show you the nearest shops this weekend?
Yes, I still haven't found a place that sells fresh bread.
There's a bakery behind the small market, but it closes at noon.
Let's go early on Saturday so I can pick up breakfast.

l2-089.title: Wishing you had studied earlier.
signature: I'm thinking of giving up French because I started late.
I wish I had studied French when I was in high school.
Then let's both join the beginner conversation group.
Do you know what we'll talk about in the first session?
Introductions and simple questions; we can prepare two each.
I'll practise giving a short answer and asking the question back.

l2-090.title: Being interrupted just before leaving.
signature: Why did Tom miss the first bus?
Tom was about to leave when Mary knocked on the door.
She probably needed to ask him something. Did he take the next bus?
Yes, he caught one ten minutes later but missed his connection.
Could he use the same ticket for the later train?
The clerk let him change it because he hadn't used it yet.

l2-091.title: Deciding if an item is too expensive.
signature: The larger lamp is sixty dollars.
The smaller one costs thirty-five and takes the same bulb.
Does the smaller one give enough light to read by?
Let's turn it on and see how far the light reaches.
That's enough for my desk; I'll take the smaller lamp.

l2-092.title: Looking for a lost item at work.
signature: I'll check the meeting room for your notebook.
Let me know if you find anything.
I will. What colour is the cover?
It's dark green, with a small white label on the back.
There's one like that in the meeting room. Did you write your name inside?
Yes, on the first page. Could you leave it on my chair if it's mine?

l2-093.title: Someone insists on paying.
signature: Did you split the bill at dinner?
Tom insisted on paying for dinner.
Let's invite him for lunch next week so we can return the favour.
Let's choose somewhere he can walk to from work.
There's a quiet place across from his office; I'll ask whether he's free on Thursday.
Good; tell him lunch is our treat this time.

l2-094.title: A final task before closing.
signature: I've printed all the labels. Can I turn the computer off?
There's something else I need you to do.
Of course. What else needs doing before we close?
Please count the returns and put them on the shelf by the office.
What should I do if the count doesn't match the list?
Write down the difference so the morning team knows what to check.

l2-095.title: Relaying a question about your teacher.
signature: What did Tom want to know after the French lesson?
Tom asked me who my French teacher was.
Tell him her beginner class is on Tuesday if he wants to join.
Does he have to register before he goes?
Yes, but he can ask for a trial session before he pays.
I'll send him the link and tell him what to bring.

l2-096.title: Too tired to talk after travelling.
signature: Did you get a chance to ask Tom about his trip?
Tom was too tired to speak.
Let's leave him to rest and ask him tomorrow.
I'll put some water in his room in case he wakes up thirsty.
Good idea; let's keep breakfast flexible so he can sleep in.
I'll leave a note so he knows where everything is in the morning.

l2-097.title: Talking about how long writing took.
signature: Was the letter hard to finish?
It took me three hours to write the letter.
Next time, we can start from the example we saved.
Which part of the example can we keep?
Keep the headings, but replace the details with this week's figures.
I'll set up a blank copy so we don't accidentally send old numbers.

l2-098.title: Politely changing the subject.
signature: We've already talked about the timetable.
Would you mind if I change subjects?
Not at all. What would you like to talk about?
Could we talk about how the course went instead?
Sure. Which activity helped you speak the most?
The one where we had to solve a problem together without reading a script.

l2-099.title: Checking how soon a task is due.
signature: Could you upload the form when you have a moment?
Do I have to do it right away?
No. Before the end of the day is fine.
Would you like the whole file or just the updated page?
Send the updated page first so I can check the change.
All right, I'll send the whole file once you confirm it.

l2-100.title: Borrowing a classmate's notes.
signature: I missed the first half of the lecture yesterday.
Of course. I'll send you a scan this afternoon.
Could you include the example at the bottom of the page?
Yes, I'll mark it so you can find it quickly.
Thanks, I'll try it on my own and ask you about any step I can't follow.

l2-101.title: Asking the way to the station.
signature: Can you tell me how to get to the train station?
Take the first left after the library. The station is at the end of that street.
Thanks. Is it close enough to walk?
Yes, it's about a ten-minute walk if you cross at the lights.
Will I see the ticket office when I come in?
Use the main entrance; the ticket office is straight ahead.

l2-102.title: Asking what an abbreviation means.
signature: This label says EC. Have you seen it before?
It can mean different things. Let's check the key at the bottom of the page.
Here it says that the letters stand for the delivery date.
That explains why this column has a different date from the invoice.
I'll write the full words on our copy so the next person doesn't have to guess.

l2-103.title: Choosing a restaurant for dinner.
signature: Have you ever been to that Japanese restaurant on Park Street?
Yes. It's quiet and the menu has several vegetarian dishes.
What time does the restaurant close?
At ten. I'll ask if they have a table at seven.
Could you ask if they have somewhere quiet for four people?
Yes, I'll request a table away from the kitchen and confirm the booking.

l2-104.title: Checking the first payday.
signature: I've finished setting up your staff account. Do you have any questions?
On the last working day of the month. The date is on your staff calendar.
What if that day is a public holiday?
Then we'll pay on the previous working day; the date will be updated on the calendar.
Thanks, I'll check the calendar before I set up my monthly payments.

l2-105.title: Borrowing a ruler in class.
signature: Certainly. Please put it back in the tray when you're done.
I will. I just need to draw a straight line.
Use the long side so the line reaches both edges.
Good point; I was about to draw it in two parts.
When you're done, pass the ruler back to me; I still need it.

l2-106.title: Agreeing on a pickup time.
signature: When should I come pick you up tomorrow?
My flight lands at four, but I'll need time to get my bag.
I'll be outside at half past four. Text me if the flight is late.
Can we meet by the short-stay car park instead of the main doors?
Yes, call me when you've collected your bag and I'll drive over.
I'll send you the exit number once I see the sign.

l2-107.title: Asking for an approximate repair price.
signature: We can replace the broken zip instead of selling you a new bag.
About how much will it cost?
Around twelve dollars. I'll confirm the price before we start.
Does that cover the new part as well as the work?
It does, unless we find that the whole switch needs replacing.
Please call me first if the price is going to be higher.

l2-108.title: Heating lunch in the office.
signature: There's a microwave beside the sink.
How long should I microwave this?
Start with one minute, then stir it and check the temperature.
Should I leave the lid on while it heats?
Put it on loosely if the container is safe for the microwave.
Good, I'll use this glass bowl instead of the plastic box.

l2-109.title: Meeting again after years apart.
signature: I think the last time we met was at your graduation.
How long has it been since we last met?
Almost five years. Let's sit down and catch up.
What has changed most for you since we last met?
I moved closer to my family and started working from home twice a week.
That sounds like a good change; do you still make time for cycling?

l2-110.title: Asking when dinner is served.
signature: Welcome. You can leave your bags in the hall.
What time will dinner be served?
At seven. We've left time for everyone to arrive first.
Can I put the salad out now, or should it stay in the fridge?
Leave it in the fridge and set the plates out instead.
I'll put out an extra plate in case our neighbor joins us.

l2-111.title: Asking to speak in private.
signature: You said you wanted to discuss the schedule. Shall we talk here?
Of course. The small meeting room is free.
Could we use it for ten minutes before the next meeting?
Yes, it's free until three; I'll close the door for us.
Thank you. I'd like to discuss the schedule before it goes to the team.

l2-112.title: Choosing a way to keep warm.
signature: It's getting cold in here. The heater is already on.
Would you mind closing the window?
Not at all. I'll close it and leave the door open.
Thanks; the draft from the window was hitting my desk.
Does it feel better now, or would you rather move your chair?
It's better now. We can open the window again after the room warms up.

l2-113.title: Checking if a message was meant for you.
signature: I saw your note asking me to come by.
Did you want to tell me something?
Yes. I moved tomorrow's meeting to the smaller room.
Does everyone who was invited know about the move?
Most do, but two people haven't opened the update yet.
I'll send them the room number in a separate message.

l2-114.title: Choosing how to pay.
signature: How would you like to pay?
By card, please. Could I have a receipt as well?
Certainly. Would you like it printed or sent by email?
Printed, please; I need to hand it in with my expenses.
Here you are. Your card payment went through.

l2-115.title: Finding a cash machine.
signature: Yes, there's one next to the station entrance.
Thanks. Does it accept cards from abroad?
Yes, but check the fee before you confirm the withdrawal.
If it's too high, is there another machine nearby?
There's one inside the shopping center, next to the elevator.

l2-116.title: Ordering a drink with a meal.
signature: You've ordered the soup and the sandwich.
What do you want to drink with your meal?
Water, please. No ice, if that's possible.
Of course. Would you like it now or with the food?
Now, please; my friend will order a drink when she gets here.
I'll bring the water and leave the drinks menu on the table.

l2-117.title: Putting the rest of a task off.
signature: We've checked most of the entries, but the last page will take a while.
Can't we wait until tomorrow to finish this?
Yes, the report isn't due until Friday. We'll finish it after lunch tomorrow.
Can we save a copy now so we don't lose what we've done?
Yes, put it in the shared folder and include the date in the name.
I'll also note which sections still need figures.

l2-118.title: Checking whether entry is allowed.
signature: I need to collect a folder from this room.
Am I allowed to be in here?
Only with a staff member. Wait here and I'll go in with you.
Thanks. I'm only here to collect the box by the shelves.
All right, keep to the marked path and I'll show you where it is.
I'll check the label before I carry it out.

l2-119.title: Suggesting a different day.
signature: I can't make it on Saturday. I've already promised to help my sister.
Sunday works. Let's meet at the same place at eleven.
Will the cafe be open by then?
Yes, but we can wait by the library if it's too crowded inside.
I'll text you when I arrive so we both go to the same place.

l2-120.title: Asking for a concrete example.
signature: Explain a problem you solved and what you learned from it.
Can you give me an example?
You could describe a time when a plan changed and you had to find a new solution.
Could I use the time our delivery didn't arrive before the event?
Yes; explain how you found enough supplies and what happened in the end.
I'll mention that I checked with two nearby shops and got everything by noon.

l2-121.title: Finding the right tone in an interview.
signature: You don't need to memorise an answer word for word.
Name the situation first, then explain what you did.
How do I talk about the team without making it sound like I did everything?
Say what the team achieved, then describe your own part in it.
I'll say we met the deadline and that I arranged the final checks.

l2-122.title: Asking someone to introduce you.
signature: Can you introduce me to the girl talking with Tom?
Yes. Her name is Lina and she organises the workshops.
Thanks. I'd like to ask her about the photography session.
She runs that session; are you interested in the beginner group?
Yes, I'd like to know if I can use my phone instead of a camera.
Let's ask her now, before she starts setting up.

l2-123.title: Checking that instructions are understood.
signature: First, save a copy. Then add the date to the new file.
Do you understand what you have to do?
Yes. I'll leave the original as it is and work on the copy.
Good. How will you make sure we know which version you edited?
I'll put today's date and my initials in the new file name.
That's clear; send me the link when the changes are ready.

l2-124.title: Asking where to put your coat.
signature: Come in. Everyone's in the sitting room.
Where should I put my coat?
On the hook by the door. There's a free one on the left.
Thanks. Is it all right if I leave my wet umbrella there too?
Put the umbrella in the stand so the floor stays dry.
Good idea. I'll shake off the extra water outside first.

l2-125.title: Checking your technique.
signature: Hold the paper here and fold along the dotted line.
Almost. Line up these two corners before you press the fold down.
Like this? The edges are even now.
Yes, press from the middle outwards to make a clean fold.
That looks better; I'll use the same method on the second sheet.

l2-126.title: Talking about your Saturday morning.
signature: What time do you usually get up on Saturday?
At around eight. On weekdays I get up at six.
Let's have breakfast at nine, then.
Do we have time to stop at the market afterwards?
Yes, if we go straight there before it gets busy.
I'll take a bag so we don't have to buy one there.

l2-127.title: Choosing between two devices.
signature: The smaller tablet is lighter, but the other has a longer battery life.
Which one do you think I should buy?
I'd choose the lighter one if you'll be carrying it every day.
Will the lighter one last a whole day without charging?
Only if you don't use it heavily; the larger one has a better battery.
Then I'll take the larger one. I often work where there isn't a socket.

l2-128.title: Suggesting it's time to leave.
signature: The last bus leaves in twenty minutes.
Yes. Let's thank our hosts before we head to the stop.
Do we have time to help clear the table first?
Yes, but we should leave in five minutes to catch the bus.
I'll take the plates in, then meet you by the front door.

l2-129.title: Opening a meeting on a positive note.
signature: We have two updates today, one good and one difficult.
Let's start with the good news.
The new timetable was approved this morning.
That's good news. When will people start using it?
On Monday, but we need to share the changes before Friday.
I'll draft a short note highlighting the shifts that moved.

l2-130.title: Disagreeing respectfully on a plan.
signature: I think we should send the new form to everyone at once.
I don't agree with you on this point.
Would you prefer to try it with one team first?
Yes, then we can see how much extra work it creates.
Which team could try it without disrupting their busiest days?
Let's ask the morning team to test it on a quiet Wednesday.

l2-131.title: Clearing up who paid.
signature: Did Sara pay the whole bill before we left?
It was me who paid the bill.
Thanks. I'll send you my share when I get home.
Could you wait until I send you the total?
Sure, but leave out the tea I didn't order.
I will; I'll send a photo of the receipt with your share marked.

l2-132.title: Checking before leaving the kitchen.
signature: I've washed the last pan. Can we leave now?
See if the gas is turned off.
It's off. I'll switch the light off too.
Did you leave the window open to let the steam out?
Yes, but it's clear now, so we can close it.
I'll close it while you check that the back door is locked.

l2-133.title: Getting oriented in a new city.
signature: Do you already know your way around Boston?
I've never been to Boston before.
Then let's start with the map and mark your hotel.
Could you mark the nearest bus stop too?
It's here, across from the hotel; take the bus that says city center.
Great, I'll save a photo of the map so I can check it later.

l2-134.title: Complimenting a homemade dish.
signature: I tried a new recipe for the rice.
Thank you. I added lemon and fresh herbs.
Do you add the lemon while it cooks or at the end?
At the end; it tastes fresher that way.
I'll try that next time. Could you write down which herbs you used?

l2-135.title: Asking for a final extension.
signature: How much extra time would make a difference?
All I need is three more days.
All right. Send the draft on Friday so we can review it before Monday.
I'll send the sections that are ready and mark the one that still needs checking.
Can you include a note explaining when the missing information will arrive?
Yes, I've asked for it by Friday morning and will let you know if it slips.

l2-136.title: Reporting an offer of a taxi.
signature: What did Tom say when he saw you waiting outside?
Tom asked if I needed a taxi.
That was kind of him. Did you take a taxi or wait for the bus?
We waited for the bus because the sign said it was only five minutes away.
Did you have enough time to make your connection?
Yes, but next time I'll check the live times before I turn down a ride.

l2-137.title: Reassuring someone about time.
signature: I still need to check the final slide. How long until we start?
Good. I'll rehearse the ending once before we go in.
Do you want me to tell you when you have one minute left?
Yes, raise your hand so I can see without stopping.
All right. I'll time it from the moment you start speaking.

l2-138.title: Sorting out a booking error.
signature: My ticket says seat twelve, but this one has a different name on it.
Could you check both tickets before we move anyone?
One ticket shows Friday, but the other shows Saturday.
Can we change the Saturday ticket without losing the seat?
I'll check whether that seat is still free on Friday.

l2-139.title: Reporting a question about a purchase.
signature: What did Tom ask Mary when she showed him the car?
Tom asked Mary when she had bought her car.
She bought it last month. Tell him she can show it to him tomorrow.
Would she mind bringing the receipt so he can see what it cost?
I'll ask her; the shop might have changed the price since then.
Good point. I'll check today's price before I decide to buy one.

l2-140.title: Finding something you thought was lost.
signature: Did Tom have to call a locksmith after all?
Tom found the keys he thought he had lost.
That's a relief. Where had he left them?
In the side pocket of the bag he took to work.
Did he tell the office he no longer needs a spare set?
Yes, and he put a bright tag on his keys so they're easier to spot.

l2-141.title: Making a room bright enough to study.
signature: I'll move the lamp closer to the desk.
Thanks. Now I can see the small print.
Is the light shining directly on your screen now?
A little; could you turn the lamp towards the wall?
Like this? You can still move it closer to the book if you need to.

l2-142.title: Sorting items for washing.
signature: Shall I put this scarf back in the drawer?
All right. I'll check the label and put it with the other scarves.
Does the label say to wash it in cold water?
Yes, and it says not to put it in the dryer.
Let's hang it on the small rack so we remember to take it out.

l2-143.title: Choosing a place to camp.
signature: How about this flat area beside the path?
This looks like a good spot to set up camp.
Let's check whether camping is allowed here before we unpack.
The sign says we need a permit. Can we get one here?
There's an office by the gate; ask which areas are open tonight.
If this area is full, I'll ask about a spot closer to the road.

l2-144.title: Helping someone keep up in class.
signature: Why has Tom stopped volunteering answers in class?
Tom finds it difficult to keep up with the rest of the class.
Let's give him a copy of the questions before the next lesson.
Could we also show him how we take notes during the discussion?
Yes, let's give him an example with only the key words.
I'll bring a blank copy so he can try it himself.

l2-145.title: Giving someone just what they need.
signature: I brought you a phone charger. I remembered yours had stopped working.
This is just what I needed.
Try it here before you go. The cable is in the box.
The screen is on, but how can I tell whether it's charging?
Look for the small symbol beside the battery level.
I see it now; thanks for checking that this cable fits my device.

l2-146.title: Finding material for a project.
signature: I need a book on local history. Where should I look?
There are many books on this subject.
Could you recommend one with pictures and short chapters?
This one has photos on every page, and the index is easy to use.
Could I take a copy of the map for my notes?
Yes, use the scanner near the desk and keep the page number for your reference.

l2-147.title: Deciding where to start reading.
signature: Should we read the introduction or jump straight to the examples?
Let's begin with the first chapter.
Good idea. We'll each bring one question to our next meeting.
Should we stop at the end of the first chapter?
Yes, then we can discuss why the main character left home.
I'll mark the paragraph that first made me wonder about that.

l2-148.title: Questioning an offer that sounds suspicious.
signature: The seller wants me to send money before I see the item.
I'll ask to see it first. If they refuse, I'll leave it.
Ask for the model number too, so you can check what it's worth.
If the number doesn't match the listing, I won't hand over any money.
Good; take your time and walk away if you feel pressured.

l2-149.title: Deciding whether to wait.
signature: Tom is getting the key. Shall we go to the room now?
Let's wait till he comes back.
Okay. I'll lay out the papers while we're here.
Put the blank forms here so people can start while they wait.
What if the person we're waiting for doesn't come by noon?
We'll leave the forms with reception and come back after lunch.

l2-150.title: Checking if the window can be opened.
signature: It's a little stuffy in this room.
Do you mind if I open the window?
Not at all. Open it just a little, please.
Is this enough, or would you like a bit more air?
That's enough. Could you move the papers away from the window?
I'll put them in this folder so they don't blow away.

l2-151.title: Offering to show someone how.
signature: I haven't used this printer before.
Let me ask you a simple question.
Of course. Do you want to know which size I need?
Yes, and show me how to measure it before I cut anything.
Measure from this edge, then leave a little extra for the fold.
I'll mark the line in pencil and ask you to check it.

l2-152.title: Leaving earlier to avoid the rush.
signature: Should we leave at noon or wait until after lunch?
The sooner you leave, the better.
All right. I'll pack lunch so we can leave before noon.
Do you think we'll find parking if we arrive at one?
Probably, but there's a second car park behind the station if the first is full.
I'll save both locations so we don't have to look them up on the way.

l2-153.title: Reporting a broken door.
signature: Why did you move the meeting to the other room?
One of the doors was broken.
Thanks for letting me know. I'll tell the people who haven't arrived yet.
Should I put a sign on the door as well?
Yes, write which entrance to use until this one is fixed.
I'll put an arrow on it so people don't have to stop and read much.

l2-154.title: Finding a connection at school.
signature: Do you know anyone in the new reading club?
Tom goes to the same school as I do.
Great. Could you ask Tom which room the club uses?
Yes. Do you want me to ask when new members can visit?
Please do; I can come after school on Wednesday or Thursday.
I'll send you the room number once he confirms the day.

l2-155.title: Writing a first letter in French.
signature: Would you like me to read your letter before you send it?
This is the first time I've ever written a letter in French.
Then let's check the greeting first and keep the rest simple.
How do I greet someone I haven't met before?
Use a formal greeting and explain in one sentence why you're writing.
I'll draft the first two lines and then read them back to you.

l2-156.title: Finishing an outdoor task before the heat.
signature: Shall we move the plants this afternoon?
Let's do this before it gets hot.
You're right. We can move them now and water them later.
Where should we put the pots until then?
Leave them beside the wall where they'll get shade at midday.
I'll move the smallest ones first and come back for the heavy ones with you.

l2-157.title: Focusing on today's priorities.
signature: We have a long list of jobs and only two people today.
Let's concentrate on what needs to be done today.
The orders that go out this afternoon should come first.
One of those orders is missing a label. Who can print it?
I'll print it while you check the delivery addresses.
Then I'll put the urgent orders on the top shelf so the driver sees them first.

l2-158.title: Agreeing with one point.
signature: We should try the new schedule with one team before asking everyone to switch.
I agree with you on that point.
Great. Let's ask the morning team to try it next week.
What should they record while they try it?
Ask them to note how long each step takes and what they find confusing.
I'll make a short form so we can compare their answers on Friday.

l2-159.title: Relaying a question from reception.
signature: What happened when you got to the front desk?
Tom asked me what I wanted.
Did you tell Tom you had come to collect the key?
Yes, and he said the key was in an envelope with my name on it.
Did he ask you to sign for it?
Yes, and I left my number in case they need the key back early.

l2-160.title: Describing what someone wore.
signature: What did Tom wear to the interview yesterday?
Tom was wearing a gray suit and a red tie.
I might wear my dark blue jacket when I go.
Will it be warm enough if we have to wait outside?
I'll take a scarf as well; it was colder than I expected last time.
Good idea. You can leave both on the rack once we're inside.

l2-161.title: Offering help for next time.
signature: I stayed late to put all the figures into the spreadsheet.
I could have helped you with your work.
Thanks. I'll ask next time instead of trying to do it all myself.
Which part took you the longest this time?
Checking the figures; I had to open three different files.
Next time, send me one of the files and we'll check them in parallel.

l2-162.title: Estimating whether someone will come.
signature: Should we keep one more seat free?
It's quite likely that Tom will come.
I'll save one by the door so he can get in easily.
Could you tell him which entrance is closest to his seat?
Yes, I'll send him a picture of the side door.
Good. If he can't make it, we can give the seat to someone else.

l2-163.title: Describing a way to learn English.
signature: My brother practised short conversations every evening.
This is the way he learned English.
Then I'll try one short conversation after dinner each day.
Try repeating the conversation with a different detail the second time.
For instance, I could change the time when I book a table.
Exactly, and ask a new question so you practise listening to the answer too.

l2-164.title: Reporting an apology for being late.
signature: What did Tom say when the meeting had already started?
Tom apologized to Mary for being late.
Good. I'll send him the notes from the first ten minutes.
Could you highlight the decision he needs to act on?
Yes, I'll put it at the top and add the deadline.
Great, then he can catch up before the next meeting.

l2-165.title: Making room for extra practice.
signature: We still hesitate when we reach the last two slides.
All we need is a little more practice.
Let's run through those two again before we finish.
Can I try the second one without looking at the script?
Yes, I'll play the other speaker and change the question slightly.
Good; if I get stuck, let me finish before you correct me.

l2-166.title: Checking approval before a change.
signature: Did the building manager agree to the new sign?
Let's wait for the reply before we order it.
Is there anything we can prepare without approval?
We can confirm the quantity and ask how long delivery takes.
I'll get those details ready so we can place the order as soon as we hear back.

l2-167.title: Reporting a request to open a window.
signature: Why is the window open when the room is empty?
Tom asked me to open the window.
Could you check whether he still needs it open before we leave?
He's already gone downstairs. Should I call him?
Yes; if he's finished, close it so rain doesn't come in overnight.
He said I can close it now. I'll check the latch before I go.

l2-168.title: Arriving early for good seats.
signature: The show starts at eight, and the seats aren't numbered.
Let's go to the theater early so we can get good seats.
Good idea. We can meet by the theatre at half past seven.
Do we need to collect the tickets before we go in?
No, they're on my phone; we can go straight to the entrance.
I'll bring a copy too, in case your battery runs low.

l2-169.title: Passing on a question about a meeting.
signature: Did Tom say why he called while I was at lunch?
Tom wondered when the meeting would start.
Please tell him it starts at two, and send him the link.
Should I send the agenda in the same message?
Yes, ask him to look at the second item before we start.
I'll mention that he can reply beforehand if he can't join.

l2-170.title: Choosing the best time to visit.
signature: Would it be better to visit Boston in spring or in summer?
This is the best time of year to visit Boston.
Then I'll keep the dates we picked in May.
Does anything close on the first day we're there?
The museum is closed on Monday, but the market will be open.
Let's do the market first and book the museum for Tuesday.

l2-171.title: Talking about a habit that changed.
signature: Why does Tom bring lunch to work now?
Tom used to eat out every day, but he can't afford to anymore.
Maybe we can swap simple lunch recipes.
I make a rice salad that stays fresh until noon.
Could you send me the recipe and tell me how you pack it?
Sure, I keep the dressing in a small jar and add it just before eating.

l2-172.title: Moving a conversation somewhere quieter.
signature: How was the café for your group meeting?
It was so noisy that we couldn't talk.
Let's try the library meeting room next time.
Can we book it for the same time next week?
I'll check now; it usually fills up after school.
If it's taken, let's meet earlier rather than go back to the noisy cafe.

l2-173.title: Explaining why you left a job.
signature: My shifts changed every week, and I couldn't keep my evening course.
This is why I quit the job.
What kind of schedule would let you keep studying?
I'd need two evenings free each week to attend class.
Have you asked whether the new team can offer fixed shifts?
I'll ask in the interview and explain which evenings I need.

l2-174.title: Finding a first step on a hard problem.
signature: Have you tried drawing a diagram for the last question?
I can't figure out how to solve this problem.
Start by drawing the two distances you know. Then label the one you need.
Should I draw it to scale or just show the relationship?
A rough sketch is enough; write the units next to each number.
Now I can see which distances I need to add first.

l2-175.title: Checking a bicycle before a ride.
signature: I heard a click when I pushed this bicycle out of the garage.
There's nothing wrong with this bicycle.
Then the sound may have come from the garage door. Let's check.
It still makes the noise when I push the bike outside.
Spin the front wheel slowly and see if it rubs against the brake.
It does; let's get the brake checked before we go for a ride.

l2-176.title: Getting useful advice from a colleague.
signature: Did you ask Tom how to handle the calls on your first day?
What was the one thing that helped you most?
She told me to repeat the request back before I started working on it.
Did that help you catch mistakes?
Yes, yesterday we found we were talking about two different dates.

l2-177.title: Pointing out an error on a receipt.
signature: The receipt shows three lamps, but I only bought two.
There seems to be a mistake.
I'll check the items and correct the total for you.
Thanks. I think this item was scanned twice.
You're right; I'll remove the duplicate and print a new receipt.
Could you show me the corrected total before I pay?

l2-178.title: Finding more chances to speak.
signature: How can I hear more natural speech after class?
The best way to learn a language is to live in a country where it's spoken.
I can't travel this year, but I can join a local conversation group.
Pick one that meets regularly and gives everyone time to speak.
There's a group on Thursdays that works in pairs.
That sounds promising. Ask if you can join a session before you sign up.

l2-179.title: Making a formal introduction.
signature: Welcome to the panel. Please take a seat.
Of course. Please tell us your name and the role you're applying for.
I'm Sara Ahmed, and I'm applying for the customer service role.
Thank you. Could you tell us a little about your current work?
I help people change their bookings and answer questions by phone.

l2-180.title: Inviting someone to choose an outfit.
signature: I've put the outfits for the family event in this room.
Thanks. I'll pick something I can also wear to work.
Try the plain jacket; it goes with both pairs of trousers.
It fits well. Is the fabric light enough for summer?
Yes, and you can wear a warm layer underneath when it gets cooler.

l2-181.title: Reporting a question about the weekend.
signature: Mary mentioned a market but didn't say which town she visited.
Tom wondered where Mary had spent the weekend.
I'll ask her which market it was when I see her.
Could you ask whether the food stalls are open on Fridays?
Yes, I'll ask about the opening hours and how to get there by bus.
Thanks; if it opens early, we can go before it gets crowded.

l2-182.title: Explaining why someone came.
signature: Why did Tom come to the workshop instead of calling?
Tom came here to ask us to help him.
Let's ask him to show us what he needs before we close.
He needs a copy of the booking form, not the price list.
Do we have any forms left at the desk?
Only one. I'll make a copy for him and print more for tomorrow.

l2-183.title: Planning around morning traffic.
signature: Can we drive across town at eight tomorrow?
There's a lot of traffic here in the mornings.
Then we'll take the train and walk from the station.
How long is the walk once we get off?
About twelve minutes if we use the west exit.
I'll check which carriage stops closest to that exit.

l2-184.title: Telling how you became friends.
signature: How did you get to know your friend from Taiwan?
I became friends with him while I was in Taiwan.
Do you still keep in touch now that you live in different places?
Yes, we still call each other on the first Sunday of the month.
What do you talk about now that you don't work together?
We swap news about our families and plan a walk whenever we're in the same town.

l2-185.title: Planning for a late arrival.
signature: Shall we start the reading group as soon as everyone is here?
There's a chance Tom will be late.
Let's start with a short recap. Tom can join the main discussion when he arrives.
Could someone send him the recap so we don't repeat it later?
I'll send the three key points as soon as we've agreed on them.
Good, then he can go straight to the question we're discussing.

l2-186.title: Respecting a donor's privacy.
signature: Should we put the names of the donors on the thank-you board?
The person who donated this money wishes to remain anonymous.
Then we'll write a general thank-you and leave the name off.
Should we mention what the donation will pay for?
Yes, say it will provide books without saying who donated.
I'll also keep any personal details out of the photo caption.

l2-187.title: Explaining a simple control.
signature: How do I start printing the labels after I've chosen the size?
All you have to do is push this button.
That's easy. I'll try with one label first.
Check the preview before you press the green button.
The text is too close to the edge; can I make it smaller?
Yes, use the size setting and print again once the whole line fits.

l2-188.title: Reporting a lunch suggestion.
signature: Why are Tom and Mary looking at that map?
Tom asked Mary where she wanted to go for lunch.
There's a quiet place by the park if they'd like to eat outside.
Do they need to reserve an outdoor table?
Probably on a Friday; I'll call and ask whether there's room for six.
Tell them we'll need a table inside if it rains.

l2-189.title: Asking for notice before a visit.
signature: I hope to visit you before the end of summer.
Let us know when you'll be coming to Boston.
I'll send you the dates once I've booked the tickets.
Please tell me the arrival time too so I can meet you.
I'll send the train number so you can check for delays.
Good. If it gets in late, I'll bring something for us to eat.

l2-190.title: Making a short request with a tag.
signature: The wind is blowing the papers off the desk.
Sure. I'll move the papers away from the window too.
Thanks, leave the top sheet out; I still need to sign it.
I'll put it beside your pen so you can find it.
Perfect. After I sign it, we can put the whole set in the folder.

l2-191.title: Encouraging a new learner to ask.
signature: I'm worried I'll ask something everyone already knows.
Don't be afraid to ask questions.
Thanks. Could we go over the first instruction again?
Sure. Look at the picture first and tell me what you notice.
I can see two people at a counter; should I describe what they're doing?
Yes, then imagine what the customer might ask next.

l2-192.title: Reporting an offer to look after a cat.
signature: Who looked after your cat when you travelled?
Tom offered to feed my cat while I was out of town.
That was kind. Would you like to thank him with me?
Yes, and I'd like to leave him clear instructions about feeding her.
Let's write down how much she eats and where we keep the food.
I'll add my number at the bottom in case he has a question.

l2-193.title: Responding to a compliment.
signature: Your explanation made that difficult example much clearer.
It's kind of you to say that.
I mean it. I can work through the next example by myself now.
Great. Tell me why you chose that answer when you've finished.
I'll read both choices aloud first so I can hear the difference.
Good idea; listen for what comes immediately after the verb.

l2-194.title: Making it just in time.
signature: Did Tom miss his train after getting stuck in traffic?
Tom barely made it in time.
Good. I'll text him the address for when he arrives.
Tell him to use the side door; the main one closes when we start.
I'll mention that and ask him to text when he's outside.
Good. I'll leave a seat free near that door.

l2-195.title: Reporting a promise about timing.
signature: Should we keep Tom's place on the morning team?
Tom promised Mary that he wouldn't be late.
Then we'll keep him on it and send everyone the start time.
Should we ask him to arrive ten minutes early to set up?
Yes, tell him which equipment will already be in the room.
I'll send him the list now so he can bring anything that's missing.

l2-196.title: Taking a discussion over lunch.
signature: We've both got ten minutes until the next meeting.
Good idea. We can use the full lunch break to work out the details.
Could we agree on the main decision before we order?
Yes, start with the budget; we can discuss dates while we eat.
I'll bring the two estimates so we can compare the costs directly.

l2-197.title: Narrowing down a misunderstanding.
signature: I've explained how the first two examples fit the rule.
There's one thing I don't understand.
Which part? Let's compare it with the shorter example.
I can't tell whether the second instruction replaces the first one.
It adds a step. Try doing the first step, then check the result before you continue.
I see the difference now; I'll number the steps in my notes.

l2-198.title: Finding who to speak to.
signature: I need to change the delivery address, but I can't do it online.
Tell me who I have to talk to.
Ask for the dispatch desk. They'll check whether the parcel has left.
Should I give them my order number or the tracking number?
Use the tracking number if you have it; it points to the exact parcel.
I'll have both numbers ready in case they need to check the order as well.

l2-199.title: Explaining a long wait for the bus.
signature: You sound tired. Are you still at the bus stop?
I've been waiting for the bus for three hours.
I'll check whether another route is running and call you back.
Could you check the bus from the stop by the library?
It leaves in twelve minutes. Can you walk there in time?
Yes, I'll head there now and tell you when I'm on the bus.

l2-200.title: Keeping a decision open to discussion.
signature: Does the draft mean the new timetable has already been decided?
Good. I'd like to suggest a later start for the evening group.
What would be the advantage of starting later?
More people could come after work, but we'd have less time in the room.
Let's ask the group which time they can manage before we book it.

l3-001.title: Finding cash near the hotel.
signature: There is a bank in front of the hotel.
Can I get there without crossing the main road?
Yes. The hotel and the bank are on the same side.
Does the machine take international cards?
It does. Just in case, keep a second card with you.

l3-002.title: Checking in for a dawn flight.
signature: What time should I check in?
The airline says to be at the airport two hours before departure.
I'll book a taxi for five, then.
It's already in my bag. Do I need a printed boarding pass?
Your phone will do. Make sure it's charged before we leave.

l3-003.title: Returning to the hotel in the rain.
signature: When did it begin to rain?
Just after we reached the lakeside path.
Luckily, Tom had an extra umbrella.
It's worth bringing your own next time.
You're right. The path is getting slippery.
Let's go back to the hotel.

l3-004.title: Walking to the guesthouse.
signature: How far are we from your house?
About ten minutes on foot, if we use the footbridge.
Only about fifty metres. There is a ramp at the far end.
That helps. My suitcase is a bit heavy.
We can take a break on the bench after we cross.

l3-005.title: Catching the next bus together.
signature: When is the next bus to Park Street?
At a quarter past six. It leaves from the stop across the road.
Can you save me a seat if you get there first?
Of course. Use the crossing by the pharmacy.
Be careful when crossing the street.

l3-006.title: Planning a short summer break.
signature: Have you decided where you're going next summer?
I haven't decided yet. I could stay near the lake or visit the coast.
I can't remember the last time I took a vacation.
Then let's choose somewhere we can reach by train.
The lake sounds good. We can go for just two nights.
I'll check the fares before we make up our minds.

l3-007.title: Checking the shared taxi fare.
signature: Do you know how much it costs?
The taxi is eighteen in total. We can split it three ways.
How much cash do you have on you?
I have enough for my share. Do you mind if I pay you after we arrive?
That's fine. I'll tell the driver there are three of us.
In that case, let's meet at the front entrance.

l3-008.title: Asking for an accessible restroom.
signature: Excuse me, can you help me?
Sure. Are you looking for something in the terminal?
Can you show me where the bathroom is?
There is an accessible one beside the lifts.
Can we get there without using the stairs?
Yes. Go straight ahead and turn right at the information desk.

l3-009.title: Deciding what to see at the lake.
signature: Where would you like to go first?
Let's start with the lakeside path while it's quiet.
There are a few boats on the lake.
Would you like to rent one after our walk?
Maybe. It depends on the weather and the price.
Let's ask at the kiosk before we decide.

l3-010.title: Finding a safe way home.
signature: How are we going to get home?
The last bus has gone. We could call a taxi from the station.
I'd rather wait inside where it's well lit.
Okay. Can you send me the driver's name when you book?
Of course. I'll also share the pickup point.

l3-011.title: Welcoming a new neighbor for tea.
signature: I didn't expect to see you here.
I just moved into the flat upstairs. My name is Sara.
I'm Omar. Please come in; I was about to put the kettle on.
Would you like a cup of tea?
Yes, please. I've heard the courtyard is open to everyone.
It is. We can take our tea outside if you'd like.

l3-012.title: Giving a friend a spare key.
signature: Thanks. Can I leave the spare with you while I'm away?
Of course. I'll keep it in this envelope.
Don't forget to lock the door.
I will. Do you want me to check the plants as well?
That would be great. Water them only if the soil feels dry.

l3-013.title: Making up after a misunderstanding.
signature: I thought you were upset about my decision.
I didn't mean to hurt you.
Thanks for saying that. I just wanted a chance to explain.
Could you please tell me what you heard?
Yes. Then we can clear up what actually happened.

l3-014.title: Thanking a friend for a favor.
signature: You could have called. Was everything okay after I left?
I appreciate what you did for me.
It was no trouble. I think you'll be fine on your own next time.
I feel more confident now. I owe you one.
You can help me carry these books next week.

l3-015.title: Recognizing an old classmate.
signature: Do you remember the first time we met?
We were waiting outside the wrong classroom, weren't we?
I was a student at that time.
So was I. I used to carry a paper timetable everywhere.
Now I put everything on my phone and still mix up the rooms.
Some things never change. Shall we catch up over lunch?

l3-016.title: Asking what someone does for work.
signature: Exactly what kind of work do you do?
I repair household appliances. Most days I work in a small shop.
How do you like your new job?
I like it. I usually spend mornings talking to customers.
I work on repairs when the shop is quieter.

l3-017.title: Checking on family from afar.
signature: How's the weather where you are?
It's quite cold this week, but we've got plenty of warm clothes.
You should take a sweater if you go out this evening.
I will. Are you still driving here on Friday?
Yes. I should be there before dark.

l3-018.title: Inviting the whole family.
signature: How about another piece of cake?
Just a small piece, thanks. Would you like to join us for lunch on Saturday?
I'd love to. Is it all right if I bring the children?
Great. Do you want me to bring a dish?
A fruit salad would be lovely, if you have time.

l3-019.title: Setting a boundary on work calls.
signature: Can I call around two to ask about the weekend plans?
Don't call me when I'm at the office.
No problem. What time do you usually finish?
At five. I'll be free after half past five.
In any case, I'll call you tomorrow.
Good. Send me a text first in case I'm still on the bus.

l3-020.title: Discussing a film without spoilers.
signature: I usually pick comedies, but there's a documentary I'd recommend.
Do you watch it in English or with subtitles?
With subtitles the first time. It was easier to follow.
Can you tell me a bit about it without giving away the ending?
It follows a group of volunteers restoring an old bridge.
I'd like to watch that. What's the title?
This is one of my favorite movies.

l3-021.title: Ordering a mild dish.
signature: Almost. Could you please tell me which dishes are mild?
The rice and grilled chicken are mild. The sauce comes separately.
I'll have that, please. Could you leave the sauce on the side?
How is everything? Is the chicken to your taste?

l3-022.title: Comparing jam and marmalade.
signature: What's the difference between jam and marmalade?
Marmalade is usually made with citrus fruit and includes pieces of peel.
That explains the slightly bitter taste. Can I try a little?
Yes. Try it on this piece of toast.
I like it. Is there enough milk left for a drink?
There's almost no milk left in the glass.

l3-023.title: Using what is in the fridge.
signature: Do you have anything in the refrigerator that I can eat?
There are some cooked vegetables and a little rice.
I don't feel like eating out this evening.
Neither do I. Let's make a quick meal with what we have.
I'll warm the rice if you set the table.
Deal. Give me a minute to wash these plates.

l3-024.title: Taking turns cooking.
signature: Whose turn is it to cook tonight?
It's my turn. I promised to make dinner on Wednesdays.
A vegetable stew. Can you chop the onions while I wash the carrots?
Sure. Which knife should I use?
Use the small one. I'll get the cutting board.

l3-025.title: Choosing a meal with guests.
signature: Yes, especially the bean dishes. What are you thinking of making?
We could serve fish tacos or a beef and bean stew.
In that case, let's make the stew and serve the toppings separately.
Great. I'll check whether anyone wants a meat-free option.

l3-026.title: Trying the homemade cake.
signature: I especially like your chocolate cake.
Thank you. I used less sugar this time.
How about another piece of cake?
Just a small one. Would you like some fruit with yours?
Yes, please. The strawberries would go well with it.
Help yourself. They're in the bowl beside you.

l3-027.title: Cleaning up after spilled milk.
signature: That's okay. Put the jug down before it spills again.
Can you pass me a cloth?
Here you are. The milk ran under the table too.
I'll wipe the floor while you move the chairs.

l3-028.title: Asking when dinner will be ready.
signature: How much time do you need to finish cooking?
About ten minutes. The rice just needs to rest.
I'll set out the plates while we wait.
Thanks. Could you put the salad on the table too?

l3-029.title: Checking on a guest after lunch.
signature: I'm glad you liked it. Would you like the recipe for the soup?
Yes, please. I couldn't tell which herbs you used.
Mostly parsley and a little mint. I'll write down the amounts.
That would be great. Thanks for having me.

l3-030.title: Remembering milk at the shop.
signature: I almost forgot to buy milk.
Good thing you remembered. We need some for tomorrow's breakfast.
Do you want a large carton or a small one?
The small one, please. The last large carton went to waste.
I'll get that and some oats. For the picnic, could we just take forks for the soup?
It's impossible to eat soup with a fork.
Then I'll pack two spoons when I get home.

l3-031.title: Comparing two chairs for home.
signature: It depends on whether you need back support or something you can fold.
This is the most comfortable chair I've ever sat in.
That one has more support, but it's heavier to move.
I'll keep it in my study, so the weight isn't a problem.
Then I'd choose that one. Take your time before you pay.

l3-032.title: Buying shoes within a budget.
signature: They're forty-five. The pair beside them is on sale today.
Would you like to try the pair that's on sale?
Yes, if you have it in my size.
We do. It's thirty, and you can return it within a week.

l3-033.title: Finding the right bag for work.
signature: Can I see a bag that fits a laptop and has a side pocket?
Try the grey one. There's a padded pocket inside.
Here you are. Try putting your laptop in the padded pocket.
This is what I've been looking for.
Would you like to test the zip before you buy it?

l3-034.title: Explaining why a purchase was costly.
signature: How much did delivery add to the price?
About twenty. I didn't see the delivery charge until the final screen.
Next time, compare the total rather than the price on the product page.
And if you can collect it yourself, you might save the whole fee.

l3-035.title: Asking about an exchange.
signature: You can exchange it for a different size, or we can refund you.
I'd like to exchange it if the larger size is in stock.
Let me check. Did you buy it online or here?
