I bought it here, but the receipt is at home.
I'll set the larger size aside while you get it.
I'm sorry to cause you all this trouble.
No trouble at all. We'll hold it until closing time.

l3-036.title: Choosing a book as a gift.
signature: What kind of books do you read?
Mostly travel writing and short biographies. I'm buying for my brother today.
Do you know if he likes books with photographs?
Yes. These two both have pictures.
The one with the short chapters. It's easier to read on a commute.

l3-037.title: Deciding whether to buy a secondhand bike.
signature: Almost everyone I know has a bicycle.
I'm thinking of buying one secondhand, but I don't know what to check.
You should try the brakes and see whether the frame fits you.
Squeeze each brake gently while you push the bike. Both wheels should stop when tested separately.
I'll ask the seller if I can take a short test ride too.

l3-038.title: Finding out what is included in the price.
signature: What else are you planning to do?
I'm comparing these printers. One looks cheaper, but it comes with no ink.
How much does the replacement ink cost?
I don't care about the price.
Even if cost isn't your main concern, make sure it's easy to find the right cartridge.
Good point. I'll check what the local shop keeps in stock.

l3-039.title: Picking up an order that is not ready.
signature: Can I collect the photo prints I ordered this morning?
We're finishing them now. The printer has been busy all afternoon.
About how long will it take?
About fifteen minutes. There's a bench by the door if you'd like to wait.
Are you almost finished with that?
Yes. These are your last two prints. I'll put everything in one envelope.

l3-040.title: Deciding when to leave the market.
signature: As soon as we pick up the vegetables. We've bought everything else.
Can you check the shopping list one last time?
Yes. We still need tomatoes, but the stall by the entrance sells them.
It's almost time to go home.
I'll get them while you take the bags to the car.

l3-041.title: Talking about learning English.
signature: How long have you been learning English?
For about a year. I can read quite well, but I still hesitate when I speak.
It's worth practising short answers aloud every day.
What if I get a word wrong?
It's okay to make a couple of mistakes.
That helps. I'll start with the questions people ask me most often.

l3-042.title: Asking a question before class ends.
signature: Of course. What would you like me to explain?
Could you clarify the difference between “used to” and “be used to”?
“Used to walk” describes an old habit. “I'm used to walking” means walking feels normal now.
That makes sense. I can say I used to drive, but now I'm used to walking.

l3-043.title: Asking for help with a school project.
signature: Can you help me with my school project?
Of course. What have you done so far?
I have the pictures. I need to write a short introduction.
Let's start with one sentence about why you chose the topic.
Can you explain this to me?
Sure. You can say what surprised you most when you read about it.

l3-044.title: Keeping a presentation simple.
signature: What's the main idea you want the audience to remember?
What matters is that they know what to do next.
All you need to do is remember these three very simple steps.
I like that opening. I can demonstrate each step with a picture.
Good. For example, show the empty form before you show the completed one.

l3-045.title: Sharing a book from the library.
signature: Thanks. I didn't expect you to finish it so soon.
It was easier to read than I thought. Can I borrow the next one too?
There are a lot of books in the library.
Great. Do you know where the short novels are?
They're on the lower shelf next to the dictionaries.

l3-046.title: Starting a second language as an adult.
signature: Is it hard to learn French?
It takes practice, but you don't need to study for hours at a time.
How long ago did you start studying French?
I started studying French three years ago.
What matters is how often you use it, right?
Exactly. I began with a five-minute conversation at lunch every day.

l3-047.title: Practising an exercise again.
signature: Can anybody tell me how to do this?
Yes. First, match each heading to a paragraph.
I matched the first two, but the last one doesn't seem to fit.
Read the first sentence of each remaining paragraph.
I see. This heading is about the cause, not the result.
All right, let's try it again.

l3-048.title: Agreeing on a revision plan.
signature: I don't have time to finish my homework.
Just the last question. I wonder if I can hand in the rest first.
Ask the teacher. In the meantime, we can look at an example together.
I get stuck when I try to do the whole page at once.
Try to read as many books as possible.
I'll start with the short examples in the workbook.

l3-049.title: Asking about a school program.
signature: Yes, I started here last term. Are you thinking of applying?
This is one of the best schools in the city.
That's what I heard too. Do you want to see the language department?
I'd like to find out whether they offer evening classes.
I'll introduce you to someone who can explain the timetable.

l3-050.title: Asking for feedback after a test.
signature: Don't worry about the results of your test.
I'm less worried about the grade than about my writing mistakes.
Could you please show me one answer you weren't sure about?
Here it is. I understood the question, but I didn't give an example.
Next time, support your point with a detail from the text.
You'd better get back to class.

l3-051.title: Setting a realistic delivery date.
signature: How long do you think it'll take?
Two days for a draft and another day to check the figures.
We told the client we'd send it tomorrow. Could you clarify which figures still need checking?
The figures in the last table. We haven't received the source file yet.
There's no way we can get this done.
We can still send the draft tomorrow and give them a date for the final version.

l3-052.title: Explaining a budget shortfall.
signature: The hall rental cost more than we expected, and ticket sales were lower.
There are a lot of things for us to think about.
What matters is whether we can reduce fixed costs next time.
We could hold the event in a smaller room and sell tickets in advance.
Let's estimate both savings before we propose it.

l3-053.title: Showing a colleague the new process.
signature: Open the form, enter the order number, and attach the invoice.
This is quite new to me.
Let me walk you through the first one.
Thanks. What happens if I enter the wrong number?
You'll get a warning before the form is sent.

l3-054.title: Checking what a button does.
signature: What would happen if I push this button?
It saves the draft. The button on the right sends it for review.
Can I change it after I've sent it?
You can, unless the reviewer has already approved it.
How do you know for sure?
I tested it with a sample order yesterday. Let's do another test before we use a real order.

l3-055.title: Taking responsibility for a mistake.
signature: We can fix it. Which version did you send?
The old one. I should have checked the date before attaching it.
Send the right file and tell them to disregard the first email.
Thanks for letting me know. We still have time before the meeting.

l3-056.title: Preparing to train new staff.
signature: Some of the workers have no experience.
We can pair each new person with someone who knows the job.
In addition to showing them the tasks, we should let them try a few examples.
Agreed. A short practice task will show us what they need help with.
Let's stop talking and start working.
I'll prepare the practice files. Can you check the instructions?

l3-057.title: Checking a delayed reply.
signature: I was disappointed that you didn't call.
I'm sorry. The call cut out, so I meant to send you a message afterward.
Did you manage to send it?
Can you send it now? I still need the updated time.
I'll send it in the next few minutes.
Thanks. Can you let me know when it's sent?
Yes. I'll text you when I get confirmation.

l3-058.title: Checking whether a task can be shared.
signature: How am I supposed to do this by myself?
You don't have to do all of it alone. Which part is taking longest?
Checking the totals. Could you please go over the last two pages?
Thanks. I'll send you the source figures so you can compare them.
Send me your notes too. That will save us both some time.

l3-059.title: Planning a work trip without rushing.
signature: Do you often take business trips?
About once a month. The clients get in at nine. Do you think we'll be there before them?
In all probability, we'll arrive before them.
The earlier we arrive, the more time we'll have to check the equipment.
I'll compare the early train with the evening one.
Good. Book the one that gives us time to set up without rushing.

l3-060.title: Deciding what to discuss in a meeting.
signature: Did you come to talk about the deadline?
Which part of the plan are you concerned about?
What I mean is that the deadline is clear, but nobody owns the final check.
Let's give that item ten minutes and agree on one person to sign off.
That works. I'll put it at the top of the agenda.

l3-061.title: Explaining an allergy before an appointment.
signature: Thanks for telling me. I'll add that to your registration form.
Can I also mention a reaction I had to a medicine?
Yes. Do you remember its name?
I brought a photo of the package. Here it is.

l3-062.title: Describing a recurring headache.
signature: Do you have something to make this headache go away?
I'll ask a few questions before we decide what to do.
Could you tell me whether you need my appointment number first?
I have it here. Has this happened before?
Yes, I've had a similar headache before.
When was the last time that happened?
Last month. I noted the date on my phone.

l3-063.title: Answering questions about pain.
signature: It hurts more when I stand.
Were you able to walk here on your own?
Let me bring you a chair while we wait for the clinician.
Thank you. It started after I stepped off the bus.

l3-064.title: Asking what the clinician found.
signature: Could you clarify what you found when you examined the cut?
That's good to hear. Is there anything else you need to know about how it happened?
Thanks. I'll add that detail to your notes before we discuss the next step.

l3-065.title: Telling the receptionist you feel unwell.
signature: Please sit here. Would you like me to tell the nurse?
Yes, please. I feel dizzy when I stand up.
I'll let her know. Is there someone you'd like me to call?
My brother is outside. He doesn't know where I am.
I'll tell the nurse, and then I'll check if it's your brother.

l3-066.title: Giving an update about someone's health.
signature: So am I. Did he tell you when his next appointment is?
No. He said he'd call after speaking to the clinic.
The last time I saw him, he was very healthy.
Let me know if he asks for help getting there.
I will. For now, I'll just send him a short message.

l3-067.title: Checking whether anyone was hurt.
signature: The display stand fell when someone leaned against it.
At least no one was hurt.
That's a relief. We should move people away from the broken glass.
Can you tell the manager what happened while I keep the area clear?
Yes. I'll also ask where we should wait.

l3-068.title: Staying calm while waiting for help.
signature: The most important thing you can do now is to remain calm.
Okay. I called the building manager, but I don't know how long it will take.
Let me stay with you while we wait.
Thanks. Could you tell me if you hear someone at the door?
Of course. I think I hear footsteps now.
All we have to do is wait.

l3-069.title: Explaining a change in appetite.
signature: Recently, I don't have much appetite.
When did you start noticing the change?
Last week. I usually have breakfast, but lately I've been skipping it.
Has anything else changed in your routine?
I usually wake up at six.
I see. You still get up at the same time. Let's talk about how you're sleeping.

l3-070.title: Leaving a health appointment on time.
signature: Do you mind if I leave after we check the next appointment date?
Not at all. Your follow-up is next Tuesday at ten.
Of course. The date is on this slip. Please take it with you.
Thank you. May I come by if I need a copy of the form?

l3-071.title: Looking for keys before leaving.
signature: Where did I put my keys?
Check the shelf by the front door. You put your bag there earlier.
Look what I found under the sofa.
Are those your keys or the spare set?
They're mine. I'll put them by the door from now on.
Good idea. We won't have to search for them tomorrow.

l3-072.title: Checking the house before leaving.
signature: Make sure the door is locked.
I'll check it. Can you turn off the lights upstairs?
Done. Did you close the kitchen window?
No rush. I'll take the bags out to the car while you check.
All done. We can leave now.

l3-073.title: Finding a place for everyday items.
signature: Where should I keep the charger so we can both find it?
There is a basket there already. I'll put the charger inside it.
Good. And where are you going to put your glasses?
I'll keep them in the case by the lamp.
Don't leave your glasses on the table.

l3-074.title: Saving the rest of the work for tomorrow.
signature: You should leave the rest of the work for tomorrow.
You're right. I only need to save the file before I close the laptop.
I'll turn off the hallway light. Do you want it left on for anyone?
Okay. I'll leave a note by the door so we remember the file in the morning.

l3-075.title: Agreeing when to stop a game.
signature: I know. I was disappointed because I thought I could win this round.
Let's finish this round and take a break.
Sounds good. I'm getting hungry anyway.
Let's continue the game after supper.
Great. Leave the pieces where they are so we can pick up from here.

l3-076.title: Choosing a quieter place to talk.
signature: It is. Would you mind moving to the table by the window?
I don't mind at all. I can't hear you from here.
It's still a bit loud. Shall we go outside instead?
I think that's a great idea.
Let's take our drinks with us and sit on the bench.

l3-077.title: Checking a computer that will not start.
signature: There's something wrong with my computer.
Can you tell me what happens when you turn it on?
The power light comes on, but the screen stays dark.
Is the charger connected firmly? We can check the simple things first.
I'm trying to figure out what's wrong.
Let's make a note of what we've tried in case we need to call for help.

l3-078.title: Working out where the noise came from.
signature: Was it coming from the street or from inside the building?
It sounded like something had fallen in the hallway.
What did you hear when you opened the door?
All of a sudden, a dog began barking.
There is a dog in the flat next door. It may have heard the same noise.

l3-079.title: Putting off an errand until later.
signature: There's something I need to do this afternoon.
Do you want me to come with you?
No, thanks. I just need to collect a parcel before the shop closes.
Could you collect mine too? I can send you the pickup code.
That's fine. The shop is open until eight, so we still have plenty of time.

l3-080.title: Reporting a problem with the front door.
signature: Could you please take a look at the front door? The latch won't close properly.
It started sticking after the rain yesterday.
I'll write that down for the repair team. Is it difficult to shut right now?
It's more difficult than it looks.
Then I'll ask them to look at it this afternoon. Please use the other entrance until then.

l3-081.title: Explaining why you chose a profession.
signature: Why did you become a doctor?
I come from a long line of doctors.
What made that profession feel right for you personally?
The reason is that I enjoyed explaining difficult things in a way people could understand.
Can you give me an example of when you did that?
At a community event, I helped visitors understand the appointment system without using technical terms.

l3-082.title: Describing what you learned from a challenge.
signature: What was the hardest part of training the new team?
It's one of the most difficult things I've ever had to do.
What did you change after the first session?
Instead of explaining everything at once, I asked each person to try one task.
Did that make it easier to see who needed help?
Yes. That's how I spotted the confusing steps and rewrote the instructions.

l3-083.title: Describing a result in an interview.
signature: What did you achieve during your first month in that role?
I helped reduce the time it took to answer customer emails.
How did you know the change was working?
We tracked the time for a week. For example, short questions went from two days to a few hours.
So am I. We kept checking the times to make sure the improvement lasted.
This is exactly what I wanted to happen.

l3-084.title: Talking about goals for the next role.
signature: What would you like to do in the future?
I'd like to take on more responsibility for training new staff.
What would help you get ready for that?
A chance to lead a short session and get feedback afterward.
Would you like to ask me something else?
Yes. How does your team support people who want to develop their skills?

l3-085.title: Showing how you supported a colleague.
signature: Tell me about a time a colleague needed your help.
Tom asked me to help when he was in trouble.
How did you find out what was making the task difficult?
I managed to find the problem by watching him complete one order.
And what did you do once you found the cause?
We made a checklist. By the time the next order came in, he had already tried it once.

l3-086.title: Making a short introduction for an interview.
signature: My name is Sara. Thank you for meeting with me.
Tell me a little about what you're doing now.
What experience from your studies would help you in this role?
I organize events for our student group, so I'm comfortable explaining plans and answering questions.

l3-087.title: Explaining a short employment gap.
signature: Could you clarify what you were doing between the two jobs?
I took three months off to finish a course and help at home.
Did the course help you decide what to do next?
Yes. It gave me experience with spreadsheets, which I now use at work.
What did you tell your family when you got the offer?
They must have been glad to hear that after your break.

l3-088.title: Passing on a customer's question.
signature: We need to call Tom back about the two printers.
Do you have any idea what Tom wants?
Tom wondered which one he should buy.
What did you tell him to look at first?
What matters is how often he'll need to replace the ink.
Did he ask you to check whether the shop had any cartridges left?
Yes. I'll check before I call him back.

l3-089.title: Handling a confidential request politely.
signature: Do you know what another team member is paid?
Even if I knew, I wouldn't tell you.
Fair enough. I'm trying to find the pay range for this role.
What I mean is that I can't share personal details. You can ask for the published range.
Can you tell me at least how much it usually is?
That's all I can tell you at this time.
Okay. Who should I contact to ask about the published range?
The recruitment team can help. Tell them which role you're looking at.

l3-090.title: Finding out who received a notice.
signature: Did everyone get the message about the room change?
I was the only one who knew about it.
Could you please forward the notice to the whole group now?
Yes. I didn't realize the others hadn't seen it.
Let's hope that's the last time that happens.
I'll copy the shared mailing list from now on.

l3-091.title: Checking whether school is closed.
signature: Is school still open after the water leak last night?
You don't have to go to school today.
Do you know if we have an online lesson instead?
The teacher posted a short exercise. We'll go over it tomorrow.
I'll finish it this morning and put it in my bag.

l3-092.title: Exploring how a neighborhood changed.
signature: What stood on this site before the library was built?
There used to be a prison here.
Could you tell me whether any part of the old building is still here?
Yes. One wall was kept when the new library was built.

l3-093.title: Reconsidering how to prepare for a test.
signature: How did Tom feel about his results after the test?
In retrospect, Tom wishes he had spent more time studying.
I should have spread out my own practice too. I left it all until the night before.
You can plan differently for the next one.
Would you help me make a timetable for next week?
I certainly don't mind helping you.

l3-094.title: Avoiding an impulse purchase.
signature: I bought a new notebook yesterday, and I'm already looking at another one.
The more you have, the more you want.
I know. What matters is whether I'll actually use it.
Why not wait until the first one is full?
I'll set the second one aside so you can decide without rushing.

l3-095.title: Clearing up a rumor calmly.
signature: Someone said the community centre is closing for good.
No matter who says so, it's not true.
How do you know it will open again?
The staff posted the dates. It's only closed for repairs this weekend.
I'll share the notice so people have the right information.
Don't talk about people behind their backs.

l3-096.title: Showing a visitor around the house.
signature: Thanks for inviting me. Where is the garden?
Just through the kitchen. We can go out when the rain stops.
I like the photos by the door. Were they taken here?
Yes. The one in the wooden frame was taken on the day we moved in.
That's a good picture of you.

l3-097.title: Agreeing on a plan if it rains.
signature: We can move the meeting indoors if the forecast gets worse.
If it rains, I'll send everyone the new location.
Good. Let's decide before noon so nobody travels to the wrong place.
Let me know when you're ready.
I'll check the forecast at eleven and text you then.

l3-098.title: Offering a friend a drink while they wait.
signature: Do you want me to buy you a drink?
Yes, please. Water is fine if you have some.
Would you like still water or sparkling water?
Still water, thanks. I'll wait here with the bags.
Take your time. Our bus doesn't leave for another twenty minutes.

l3-099.title: Asking for directions in an unfamiliar place.
signature: What's the name of this place?
This is Riverside Square. Where are you trying to go?
Do you know where the nearest bus stop is?
It's behind the market, just past the flower stall.
Is there any place around here where we can get something to eat?
There's a small café next to the stop. You can wait there and get something to eat.

l3-100.title: Building a plan to practise speaking together.
signature: What could we do to make our speaking practice feel more like real life?
Let's choose a situation and change one detail each time we practise.
I think that will help us answer without memorizing the whole conversation.
Exactly. You can be the customer first, and I'll ask you to explain what you need.
Tell me how to do it.
Sure. Start by saying what went wrong, then ask what your options are.
And if I get stuck, we'll try it again more slowly.
Let's see what happens this time.

l3-101.title: Making a first visit feel relaxed.
signature: How much longer are you going to be here?
Just until four. Can I leave my bag here while we go outside?
Of course. I'll put it where you can see it.
Where would you like to start the tour?
There's so much I want to show you.
Let's start in the garden, then.

l3-102.title: Introducing a friend at an event.
signature: In Aden. I moved here for work two years ago.
Do you already know anyone in this group?
Except for Tom, I didn't know anyone there.
Let me introduce you to the people at this table.
Thanks. It feels easier when I know a few names.

l3-103.title: Replying to good news.
signature: I am. I got a place on the course I applied for.
I suppose I should congratulate you.
Thanks! The first class is in two weeks.
Would you like to tell the rest of the group yourself?
Yes. I'll tell them when we meet tonight.

l3-104.title: Checking in after a long day.
signature: Did you have a rough day?
A bit. I had to finish two things at the same time.
Would you like a few minutes to yourself before we talk?
Yes, that would help. I'll sit out here for a while.
No problem. We can catch up tomorrow.

l3-105.title: Checking a story before retelling it.
signature: I heard that Tom found the lost notebook at the station.
Are you sure his name was Tom?
Now that you ask, I only heard the story from a friend.
I can't remember exactly what Tom said.
Let's ask the owner before we pass the story on.
Good idea. I don't want to tell anyone the wrong thing.

l3-106.title: Telling a joke that fell flat.
signature: Oh, I thought you were serious about cancelling the picnic.
What I mean is that we might need a different place if it rains.
Got it. Let's agree on a backup place now.
The covered tables are free in the afternoon. I'll check whether we can reserve one.

l3-107.title: Offering company to a neighbor.
signature: I never liked being at home alone.
Would you like to sit with us in the courtyard for a bit?
I'd like that. I don't know many people here yet.
Come down at six. We usually bring a pot of tea.
Thanks for inviting me. It means a lot.

l3-108.title: Explaining how you heard the news.
signature: I heard about your problems from Tom.
I'm glad someone told you. I wasn't sure how to bring it up.
Do you mind if I ask what happened after the meeting?
Not at all. They gave me another chance to explain.
That sounds fair. Were you able to say what you wanted?

l3-109.title: Thanking someone for a thoughtful gift.
signature: This is something Tom made for you.
That's kind of him. Did he make the frame too?
Yes. Look at the small pattern he carved around the edge.
I'd like to thank him in person. Do you know where he'll be this afternoon?
He'll be in the workshop. I'll take you there.

l3-110.title: Making peace over a shared space.
signature: I'd like to talk about the boxes in the shared hallway.
The last thing I want to do is cause you any problems.
I understand. What matters is that everyone can get through safely.
I'll move them into my flat this evening.
Thanks. I can help you lift the heavier ones.
Let's try to treat each other with respect.

l3-111.title: Choosing a time to meet at the station.
signature: What time are you meeting Tom?
At two thirty. He asked me to meet him by the ticket machines.
Can I meet you there too, or would that be too early?
That works. The station is usually quiet around then.
I'm on my way to meet Tom at the station right now.
Okay. Text me when you're near the entrance.

l3-112.title: Explaining why you arrived late.
signature: I had a feeling you would be late.
The usual road was closed, so I had to take a longer route.
That's all right. I think we can still make the next train.
Great. Can we use the same tickets?
Good. Let's go straight to the platform.

l3-113.title: Working out where the car is parked.
signature: Are you telling me you don't remember where you parked your car?
I know it's on the second floor, but I forgot the row.
Blue. Let's look near the entrance we used earlier.
I'll check whether I took a photo of the parking ticket.
Good. The row number might be on it.

l3-114.title: Asking whether a friend needs a lift.
signature: Would you like me to drive over and collect you?
Don't bother to pick me up at the hotel.
Are you going to take the shuttle to the station instead?
Yes, it stops outside the hotel every half hour.
That saves us a trip. Let me know when you're on board.

l3-115.title: Checking what is open on arrival.
signature: The sign says the visitor centre opens at ten. Is the door unlocked?
Can I get a map there before the tour starts?
Yes. Ask for the map with the accessible routes marked.
We'll start in the courtyard and follow the path beside the old wall.

l3-116.title: Looking for shelter on a hot day.
signature: According to the thermometer, it's 30 degrees outside.
I can't stand this hot weather.
There is a shaded bench beside the entrance.
Good. I'll sit there while you buy the tickets.
Would you like a bottle of water too?

l3-117.title: Turning back before a storm.
signature: The clouds are getting darker. Should we still go up?
It's dangerous to climb a mountain during a storm.
Then let's take the lower path back to the car.
Good. We can come back when the forecast is better.
Last time we stayed too long. The path was muddy and we lost our way.
To make matters worse, it began to rain.

l3-118.title: Asking how far a farm is.
signature: How far away is your farm?
It's about twelve kilometres from the bus stop.
How do you usually get there when you have bags to carry?
My brother usually picks me up. He drives a white van.
To the little shop by the bus stop. He'll meet us there.

l3-119.title: Explaining why you missed a tour.
signature: Did you get to the museum before the guide left?
By the time we got there, it was already too late.
If we had called ahead, they might have held our places.
Next time we should check how long the journey actually takes.
Were you able to see the exhibits without the guide?
I managed to see most of them before closing.
Needless to say, we were very tired by the end of the day.

l3-120.title: Asking about a weekend trip abroad.
signature: What do you know about Australia?
A little. I have a cousin there, but I've never visited.
I'd like to go for a short course next year. Which city would you suggest?
Start by comparing the course dates and the cost of getting there.
That makes sense. Are there any other places you hope to visit?
Sooner or later, I'll probably visit Boston.

l3-121.title: Offering a drink without caffeine.
signature: Would you like mint tea instead?
Yes, if there's no caffeine in it.
It's just mint and hot water. Would you like something to eat too?
No problem. There are dates in the bowl if you change your mind.

l3-122.title: Offering a meal to a guest.
signature: A little. I missed lunch because the bus was late.
Would you like some soup while I heat the bread?
Yes, please. Even a small bowl would be enough.
Thank you. That's very kind of you.

l3-123.title: Checking food for a guest.
signature: We have two desserts. Do you need to avoid any ingredients?
I can't eat peanuts. Could you check the package?
I will. This one is plain fruit. The other is ice cream.
In general, kids like ice cream.
I'll serve fruit first so everyone has something to eat.

l3-124.title: Finding something to eat before a trip.
signature: I don't have anything to eat.
There is a sandwich shop next to the station.
It doesn't open for another hour. Is anything open now?
We could check the small shop on the corner.
I checked yesterday. The shelves were almost empty.
Then let's buy something on the train.

l3-125.title: Keeping the kitchen tidy.
signature: Can you clear the counter while I wash these vegetables?
Sure. Where should I put the clean glasses?
On the top shelf. Leave one down here for me.
It's lemon juice. I'll use it for the salad.

l3-126.title: Choosing a snack after school.
signature: Would you like yoghurt or a sandwich?
I'll take the sandwich. Do we have anything to drink?
We have juice. It's in the blue bottle.
Give me a sip of your drink.
Of course. Pour some into a clean cup first.

l3-127.title: Preparing food for someone else's visit.
signature: What should we serve when Tom comes over?
The only thing that Tom drinks is coffee.
I prefer tea to coffee, but we can offer both.
Good idea. I'll put some fruit on the table too.
What time did he say he'd arrive?
Tom may be able to come tomorrow.

l3-128.title: Asking someone to show you a recipe.
signature: I like the bread you made. Can you show me how you shaped it?
Of course. First, make a ball and flatten it with your palm.
I'll try. Is this thin enough?
Yes. Now fold the two sides toward the middle.
Have you ever tried folding them the other way?
This is the only way I know how to do this.
Good. Tell me what you'd do differently and we'll try it on the next piece.

l3-129.title: Deciding when to finish a cooking class.
signature: Is there time to cut another piece before we clean up?
Be careful not to cut yourself.
I will. The small knife is easier to hold.
Please put it back in the tray when you're done.
Done. Shall we make another batch?

l3-130.title: Asking why a guest did not enjoy a dish.
signature: Can you promise to change the recipe if Tom doesn't like the dish?
I don't want to make any promises I can't keep.
Fair enough. Did he say what he thought of it?
Tom made it clear that he didn't like the food.
What I mean is that I'd like specific feedback before I make it again.
He said it was much hotter than he expected.
Next time, I'll serve the chilli separately so everyone can choose.

l3-131.title: Comparing a repair with replacement.
signature: The battery doesn't hold a charge anymore. The rest of it works fine.
Could you tell me whether replacing it costs less than buying a new computer?
Usually, yes. We can give you a quote before you decide.
You should think about it first.
I will. Please write the estimated cost and waiting time on the quote.

l3-132.title: Working out how much a group can spend.
signature: How much money do you have with you now?
About sixty. We should keep some for the bus fare.
How much can we spend on the gift, then?
Forty at most. We could choose something useful for the kitchen.
I'll compare these two. Do you have a preference?
I don't care which choice you make.

l3-133.title: Choosing a practical gift instead of an expensive one.
signature: Tom's been looking at the same bicycle for weeks.
Tom can't afford to buy a new bicycle.
Instead of buying a new one, we could help him fix his old bike.
That might be more useful. What does it need?
A new chain and a light. I'll ask before buying anything.

l3-134.title: Asking how much a small project needs.
signature: About how much money do you need?
Around twenty. I already have the tools.
Do you have enough wood for the shelves?
For the two short ones, yes. I'll need one more piece for the long one.
Just screws. Take one of these with you so you get the right size.

l3-135.title: Checking whether a shop has what you need.
signature: I need a warm top for tomorrow. Is the shop still open?
Yes, but it closes in ten minutes. Do you mind if I lend you something instead?
Not at all. What have you got?
It fits well. I'll bring it back after the trip.

l3-136.title: Trying to fix a toy before replacing it.
signature: The wheel has come off again. Should I buy another toy?
See what you can do with it.
Let me see if the pin still fits through the hole.
It does. There may be a spare washer in that little box.
I found one. It fits, and the wheel turns properly now.

l3-137.title: Checking a package at the counter.
signature: The box looks dented. Can I check what's inside before I accept it?
Yes. I'll note the damage on the collection slip.
I'm dying to know what's inside.
Go ahead. There's a table here where you can open it.
The smaller box inside isn't damaged. I'll check the part number.

l3-138.title: Asking someone to pick up a purchase.
signature: My order is ready, but I'm still at work.
Can you send me the pickup details? I'm near the shop.
Will you do it for me?
Of course. Does the shop need to see my ID or your order number?
Just the order number and my name.
I'll stay here until you send the details.

l3-139.title: Explaining why you do not need a refund.
signature: The parcel was a day late. Would you like us to refund the delivery fee?
At this point, I don't need money.
What matters is that the replacement arrives before Friday.
I understand. I'll check whether we can send it tomorrow.
I'm sorry to cause you all this trouble.
It's all right. I'll send you the updated delivery date in writing.

l3-140.title: Discussing a purchase you decided against.
signature: What did Tom decide about replacing his truck?
Tom abandoned the idea of buying a new truck.
Could you clarify why he changed his mind?
The mechanic said the old one could last another year after a small repair.
As strange as it may sound, what Tom said is true.
He got a second estimate, and it was almost the same.

l3-141.title: Describing a weekly school routine.
signature: Busy, but I'm getting used to the schedule.
Do you go in on Saturdays as well?
I go to school five days a week.
When do you have time to practise English?
I listen to a short conversation on the way home.

l3-142.title: Catching up after missing class.
signature: I was absent from school because of illness.
I hope you're feeling better. We only covered two pages.
Can you show me which exercises I missed?
Yes. The teacher asked us to finish the one on the right.
I can do that tonight. Is there anything else?
The next lesson is about to start. I'll show you the rest afterward.

l3-143.title: Asking for time to learn a language.
signature: How many hours a day do you study French?
Only half an hour. I usually do a little before breakfast.
I'm interested in improving my French.
Then start with a short conversation about something you do every day.
What if I can't remember all the words?
Use the ones you know and explain the rest another way.

l3-144.title: Explaining why you are still a beginner.
signature: How well do you speak French?
I'm sorry for my terrible French; I'm still a beginner.
That's fine. Let's practise asking for directions first.
Could you speak a little more slowly while I try?
Of course. Tell me the place you're looking for.
I'm looking for the nearest pharmacy.

l3-145.title: Asking how someone became fluent.
signature: How come you know French so well?
I've been studying French since I was 13.
Did you learn mainly in class or by talking to people?
In addition to taking classes, I joined a weekly conversation group.
What did you do when you couldn't think of a word?
I described what I meant using simpler words.

l3-146.title: Using examples to remember a word.
signature: I remember words better when I use them in a sentence of my own.
Could you clarify how you review those sentences later?
I cover the English and try to say it from the Arabic meaning.
I know I can do it.
Try it with three sentences today. We can check them together tomorrow.

l3-147.title: Saying what did not work for you.
signature: Frankly speaking, this novel isn't very interesting.
What made it hard to keep reading?
It has too many characters. I wonder if I could start with a short story instead.
Of course. Choose one you can finish in a sitting.
All I have is a book.
You can borrow a shorter one from me. I'll bring it tomorrow.

l3-148.title: Talking about what a story meant.
signature: I finished the story last night. Did you understand the ending?
To be honest, I don't understand it.
What I mean is that the last scene changes what we know about the narrator.
Did you notice that on your first reading?
No. I went back to the first chapter to check what he'd said.
I suspected it, but I wasn't sure until the last page.

l3-149.title: Explaining why an answer sounded wrong.
signature: You used a question word, but the word order was wrong inside the sentence.
Could you clarify what changes after “Do you know”?
Say “Do you know where the bank is?” Keep “the bank” before “is”.
That makes sense. Can I try a second example?
Try to read as many books as possible.
Try one from the short article we read today.

l3-150.title: Finishing a study session before getting tired.
signature: I was up all night reading a book.
That explains why you're struggling to concentrate.
Let's finish this one question and take a break.
Good idea. We can check the other answers tomorrow.
I'll save a copy of our notes before we leave.

l3-151.title: Asking for a later start at work.
signature: Do you have to work tonight?
Yes, but is it okay if I start half an hour later?
That depends on when Tom arrives. Did he confirm his shift?
Good. Ask him to cover the desk until you get here.
I'll message him now and confirm the change with you.

l3-152.title: Explaining an adjustment to a plan.
signature: What does he plan to do?
He wants to move the training session to Thursday.
Did he tell you why the first date didn't work?
The reason is that the room has already been booked for another event.
Tom thought it was a good idea.
Then I'll check Thursday's room availability before I send an update.

l3-153.title: Passing on a request without changing it.
signature: What do you want me to ask Tom?
Ask him if he can bring the signed form tomorrow.
Could you clarify whether he should bring the original or a copy?
The original, please. We already have a copy.
Thanks. Send him a short reminder tomorrow morning as well.

l3-154.title: Explaining a missing attachment.
signature: Did you send the minutes to the whole team?
Yes, but I think I left out the attachment.
I did. I'll send a follow-up with the file right away.
Please say which version they should use.
I remember telling you about it.
You're right. Just put the date in the subject line this time.

l3-155.title: Confirming who will take the meeting notes.
signature: He said he'd join later. Can you take notes until he gets here?
Yes. Should I write down everything or just the decisions?
Just the decisions and who will act on them.
That makes sense. I'll send them around after the meeting.
Don't be late for the meeting tomorrow.

l3-156.title: Responding when a colleague sounds upset.
signature: He may just be worried about the delay. What did he say?
He asked why we hadn't called back.
Let's tell him what's been done and what's still pending.
Would it help if I phoned him now?
Tom wants to know why you didn't call him back.
Then I'll call and apologize before I explain the delay.

l3-157.title: Explaining what happened after a breakdown.
signature: Tell me what you know about the incident.
The machine stopped just as we started the morning run.
Two people were there, but neither saw what caused it.
Let's record what we know before we suggest a cause.
I'll note the time and ask them to describe what they heard.

l3-158.title: Choosing an alternative when a room is full.
signature: The training room is full. Can we move the next session online?
Even if we can't use another room, we can record a short demonstration.
That would help people who can't attend in person.
Who could record the demonstration this afternoon?
Let Tom do that for you.
I'll ask him and make sure he has the materials.

l3-159.title: Requesting details from someone who was absent.
signature: I was on another call. What did I miss?
The manager changed the review order. I need to check who goes first.
Let's ask Tom if he knows what to do.
Good idea. He took notes during the call.
I'll contact him and send you the order once I have it.

l3-160.title: Giving an honest answer about a deadline.
signature: Will you definitely be able to finish by Friday?
I don't want to make any promises I can't keep.
What matters is which parts you can deliver by then.
I can finish the summary. The numbers depend on a file from Tom.
It's very unlikely that Tom will come.
Then let's ask him to send the file today, even if he can't attend.

l3-161.title: Explaining when a symptom began.
signature: When did you first notice the problem?
I knew that something was wrong.
What made you think that? Can you describe how you felt?
I felt dizzy when I got out of bed.
Has it happened on other days as well?
When was the last time that happened?
I mean, apart from today. We can write down the dates if you remember them.

l3-162.title: Asking about a family member's appointment.
signature: He's back home. He said the next visit was on Thursday.
Do you know where the follow-up clinic is?
It's in the same building, on the first floor.
I can take him there if he needs a lift.
There's no need to worry about Tom.
Still, I'll ask whether he would like some company.

l3-163.title: Describing an old injury.
signature: What's the worst injury you've ever had?
I hurt my ankle playing football a few years ago.
Could you clarify whether it still bothers you when you walk?
Only after a long walk. I'll mention it at my next appointment.
That's a good idea. How did you get help on the day it happened?
I called Tom from the hospital.

l3-164.title: Sharing what you know after an incident.
signature: How long did it take for the ambulance to arrive?
About twelve minutes. I wrote down when I made the call.
Could you tell me whether anyone stayed with the person while you waited?
Yes. A neighbor stayed there while I went outside to meet the crew.
Thanks for keeping a record. I'll pass those details to the coordinator.

l3-165.title: Asking what is known so far.
signature: Have they found out what caused the illness?
At present, the cause of the disease is unknown.
What matters is knowing when we'll hear more.
They said they would update us after the next visit.
I can help you write down the questions you want to ask.
I need to know you're okay.
I'm okay. Having a list will help me remember what to ask.

l3-166.title: Speaking up before a vaccination.
signature: Can you tell me what usually happens before the appointment?
The nurse explains what to expect and asks whether you have questions.
What do I have to be afraid of?
You can say you're nervous and ask for time to talk it through.
Thanks. I'll tell the nurse how I feel as soon as I go in.

l3-167.title: Checking that someone got home safely.
signature: Can you let me know when you reach home?
Of course. I'm waiting for the bus now.
If the bus doesn't come, call me. I'll come and get you.
I need to know you're okay.
I'm fine too. I'll keep my phone nearby until you get in.
I just got through the door. Thanks for checking on me.

l3-168.title: Helping a visitor find the waiting area.
signature: Let me see the address on your appointment letter.
Here it is. I can't find room seven.
You're on the right floor. The waiting area is through those doors.
Should I check in first or just sit down?
The receptionist will ask for your name and appointment time, then you can take a seat.

l3-169.title: Explaining why you left early.
signature: Tom had to go home early today.
He said he had a headache and wanted to rest at home.
I'll send him a short message to ask how he's doing.
Good idea. Let me know if he needs anything from us.

l3-170.title: Making a note before talking to a clinician.
signature: I'd like to make a list before I speak to the clinician.
Good idea. Include the dates and what you noticed each day.
I don't remember the exact date it started. Will an estimate do?
Yes. Just say you're giving an estimate.
Thanks, but I'll write it down anyway so I don't leave anything out.
I'll thank the clinician after we go over the list.

l3-171.title: Keeping in touch during a power cut.
signature: I can't imagine living without electricity.
I know. We use it for almost everything at home.
Is there a charged torch in the drawer?
Yes. I'll bring it over. Is your phone still working?
Yes, but the battery is getting low. I'll use it only for messages.
I'll walk back now. Please leave the torch by the door.

l3-172.title: Deciding where to store the boxes.
signature: Tom filled the room with cardboard boxes.
Which ones do we actually need to keep?
There are two with books and one with kitchen things.
Put the books on the shelf. I'll flatten the empty boxes.
Help me clean out the garage.
Let's clear some space there first, then put them away.

l3-173.title: Asking before moving someone else's belongings.
signature: Can I move Tom's bag off this chair?
Before doing that, you need to ask Tom for permission.
Right. I'll ask him before I touch it.
We could use the other chair for now.
I only need a place to put these books.
It doesn't bother me if you take that book.
Thanks. I'll borrow that one and leave the bag where it is.

l3-174.title: Deciding when to wake someone up.
signature: I thought we were leaving in ten minutes.
I'll get dressed now. Can I sleep a bit in the car?
Sure. I'll let you know when we're close.
Wake me up when we get to Tom's.
Okay. Bring your bag down when you're ready.

l3-175.title: Cleaning a room before guests arrive.
signature: Let's open the window and wipe the shelves first.
I'll do the shelves. Could you move the chairs away from the wall?
Sure. What should I do with the papers on the table?
Put them in the blue folder so they don't get lost.
I'll tidy my room after we finish this one.

l3-176.title: Looking at an old photograph.
signature: Look at the picture on the wall.
Is that your uncle standing by the gate?
Yes. He's the person who used to look after the garden.
Who is the child holding the red ball?
That's my cousin at her first school picnic.
He's about the same age as you.

l3-177.title: Asking for help when you cannot reach something.
signature: How are you going to get up to the roof?
I'm not going up there myself. I need to ask the building manager for help.
Good. Do you know where his office is?
Yes, but it's closed now. I'll leave him a message.
What are you trying to get down anyway?
The wind carried the towel from the clothesline. I'll explain when I call.

l3-178.title: Making a realistic plan for screen time.
signature: How much time do you spend watching TV?
What about your phone? Do you use it much before bed?
Yes. Instead of checking it in bed, I could leave it on the desk.
Try that for a week and see if it makes a difference.
I'll start tonight and keep a book by the bed.

l3-179.title: Deciding how to spend a free afternoon.
signature: Would you like to go for a walk before dinner?
Yes, but I'd rather stay close to home.
We could walk around the park and stop for tea.
Is the park still open? The gate sometimes closes early.
Good. I'll meet you outside in five minutes.

l3-180.title: Sharing what you found on the beach.
signature: Guess what I found on the beach.
Let me guess. Is it something that washed up after the storm?
Yes. It's a piece of wood shaped a bit like a boat.
Look at the marks on the side. Someone may have carved it.
I think you're right. I'll take a photo before I leave it here.

l3-181.title: Explaining what you like about your current job.
signature: Tom asked me about my new job.
How did you describe it to him?
What makes it a good job for you?
What matters is that I get to solve different problems every day.
Can you give me one example of a problem you solved last week?
I helped a customer find the right replacement part after checking two different models.

l3-182.title: Explaining why you are ready for a change.
signature: What made you apply for this position?
I'm satisfied with what I have.
I see. What do you hope will be different here?
I'd like to use my experience to train a larger team.
That makes sense. Did you get many chances to do that at your old job?
Most of my day went to customer calls. I trained new starters during quieter periods.

l3-183.title: Describing how you react to feedback.
signature: Tell me about a time someone gave you difficult feedback.
I once wrote a guide that people found hard to follow.
What was your manager's first reaction when you explained why you left out the diagrams?
I'm surprised you didn't know that.
Did you revise it straight away? What I mean is how did you decide what to change?
I asked two colleagues to try the guide and tell me where they got stuck.
And did that make a difference to the next version?
The revised guide was much clearer. I used their suggestions to rewrite the first three steps.

l3-184.title: Describing a skill you learned outside work.
signature: Could you please tell me about a skill you taught yourself?
I learned to repair a bicycle by watching someone in my family.
Did you need help the first time you tried it alone?
Yes. My brother stayed nearby until I was ready to try the next step.
At what point did you feel confident?
What did you take from that experience into your work?
I can show a new colleague one step, then let them try it on their own.

l3-185.title: Asking what success looks like in a role.
signature: What would you like to know about the first month here?
Could you tell me whether new staff work with a mentor?
Yes. The mentor checks in at the end of each week.
And what would a good first month look like?
You should be able to handle a routine request and know when to ask for help.
There are a lot of things for us to think about.
Which part would you like me to go over again?
I'll think about how my previous role prepared me for that.

l3-186.title: Answering a question you did not expect.
signature: What are you going to be in the future?
I don't expect you to understand this.
Take your time. What I mean is where you'd like to develop your skills.
In that case, I'd like to become better at explaining technical problems.
What would be your first step?
I'd ask to sit in on a few customer calls and take notes.

l3-187.title: Giving a clear answer about availability.
signature: Could you start next Monday if we offered you the role?
I have something I need to do.
Could you clarify whether you could start later that week?
Yes. I have an appointment on Monday, but I'm free from Tuesday onward.
Tuesday would work. Can you confirm by email this afternoon?
Let me know when you're ready.
I will. I'll confirm once I've checked my calendar.

l3-188.title: Checking how a change affected the team.
signature: Did the new system help the team finish earlier?
Tom tried to solve the problem.
What did Tom try first? Could you clarify which part he changed?
He moved the approval step to the start of the process.
What makes you so sure that this won't happen again?
We can't be sure yet. We'll track the next three requests and see if the delay returns.

l3-189.title: Discussing where to set up a community class.
signature: We need a place for the evening class. Could we use the hall behind the library?
Tom wishes he had a larger office.
There are two smaller rooms in the same building. Would either work?
Possibly. Let's see how many people have signed up.
Will you do it for me?
Of course. I'll check the list and measure the room before we book it.

l3-190.title: Summing up after a difficult conversation.
signature: Before we leave, can we agree on what each of us will do?
What I mean is I want to check that we're both clear about the next step.
Okay. I'll call the building manager and you can send the photos.
That sounds fair. Do you want to keep talking about yesterday as well?
Let's forget about what happened last night.
All right. Let's focus on getting the problem fixed.

l3-191.title: Comparing two ways to spend the evening.
signature: Do you like to watch movies?
Yes. I usually watch one at home on Fridays.
I often go to the movies.
Would you like to go together this time?
I'd like that. Is there anything that starts before seven?
There's a comedy at six thirty. I'll check whether there are still seats.

l3-192.title: Checking whether a space can be used for practice.
signature: Is it okay to sing here?
Yes, when the room is free. Is this for a performance?
It's just practice. Can I bring a friend to listen?
Of course. Will you need the room for more than half an hour?
I don't think so. I'll stop at six even if we haven't finished.
Let's see what happens this time.

l3-193.title: Telling someone what to do with a delivery.
signature: A delivery driver just called. Can you open the front door?
Yes. Where should I put the parcel if it arrives before you do?
Which shelf do you mean? The one by the door is full.
The one under the window. Make sure the label is facing up.
That's all right. I'll ask the driver to leave it at reception.

l3-194.title: Clarifying where visitors should wait.
signature: The group has arrived. Where do you want them to wait?
Do you know where the rest of the group is?
Tom went to meet them at the shuttle stop.
Has he left the shuttle stop yet?
Tom called to say he's on his way.
I'll wait by the main doors so he can find us easily.

l3-195.title: Asking for help without handing over the task.
signature: I can't make this chart work. Could you show me the first step?
What I mean is I want to learn to do it myself.
Fair enough. Select the two columns and then choose the chart type.
Can you explain this to me?
Yes. Choose a bar chart if you want to compare the totals by week.

l3-196.title: Discussing a noisy appliance without guessing.
signature: The fan sounds louder than it did yesterday. Did you hear it?
It only happens on the highest setting. I'll turn it off and tell maintenance.
Good. We can tell them what we heard without guessing at the cause.
I knew that something was wrong.
When did you first notice the noise? I'll write it in the report.

l3-197.title: Asking someone to repeat a useful phrase.
signature: Could you please say the last part again?
Sure. I said, “I'll let you know when I get there.”
So I can use it if I'm going to meet someone later?
Exactly. Try replacing “get there” with “finish work”.
Tell me how to do it.
Say the first part, then name the thing that needs to happen first.
I'll let you know when I finish work. Did I get it right?

l3-198.title: Asking whether a guest needs anything else.
signature: Can I get you anything before I clear the table?
Just a glass of water, please.
Here you are. Did the portion suit you?
I'm glad you liked the soup. Would you like me to write down the recipe?
Yes, please. I'd like to make it next weekend.
I'll put it in a message so you can find it easily later.

l3-199.title: Giving someone space to decide.
signature: Everyone seems to want the same venue, but I still have doubts.
It doesn't matter what I think.
It does matter. What matters is whether we can explain our concerns openly.
Okay. My concern is that the room will be too small for our group.
That's a fair point. Shall we look at a larger room before we decide?
We may still need to check the price. Let's call and ask.

l3-200.title: Practising a conversation with a new ending.
signature: This time, imagine the shop has sold out of the size you asked for.
Could you tell me whether it will be back in stock next week?
It might. If you need it sooner, I can check another branch.
You can reserve one at another branch, or I can contact you when we get more.
I'll reserve one if it can be collected today.
Good. Now let's swap roles and change the deadline to tomorrow.
All right, let's try it again.
